PSCI 3933 - History and Politics of the Middle East
A survey of Middle Eastern history and politics with an emphasis on the 19th and 20th centuries. 3 hours. As needed. Same as HIST 3933 .
PSCI 4033 - Legislative Processes

A study of the legislative process of city council, state legislature, and Congress; composition of membership, organization, and powers; and the relationship with other governmental bodies. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
PSCI 4043 - African American Politics

A study of the experience of African Americans in politics in the United States. The course includes analysis of the civil rights movement, as well as African American culture, political thought, and political participation on local, state, and national levels. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
PSCI 4053 - Comparative Public Policy

A study of the formation of public policy in developed and developing nations, alternative approaches to analyzing policy making, policy constraints, and selected public policies and decisions. 3 hours. As needed.
PSCI 4073 - American Constitutional Law

A survey, using the case method, of principles, practices, and basic features of American constitutional law with emphasis on judicial review, the role of the Supreme Court, federalism, national powers, and individual rights. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as CRJU 4073 .
PSCI 4083 - Global Issues

Analysis of selected international issues such as population, resources, conflict, communication, development, and human values, from a global perspective, emphasizing transnational and interdependent relationships. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
PSCI 4153 - History of Economic Thought

This course provides a survey of the development of economic theories. Particular emphasis is placed in developing an understanding of the relationships among economic thought, political science, contemporary philosophy, and sociological issues. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as ECON 4153 and SOC 4153 .
PSCI 4203 - Comparative Politics
A study of governing processes, policies, and contemporary political problems, comparing political systems around the world. 3 hours. Fall, alternate years.
PSCI 4213 - International Law
This course is a general study of international law, with special emphasis on the discipline of public international law. 3 hours. Fall, odd years. Same as CRJU 4213 .
PSCI 4333 - Advanced Topics in Political Science
Advanced topics in political science as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
PSCI 4343 - Advanced Topics in Political Science
Advanced topics in political science as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
PSCI 4353 - Senior Paper Research

Prerequisites: Senior standing and instructor permission.
Undergraduate research and writing of a senior paper. This course provides a capstone research experience. Although supervised by an instructor, it is expected that a student enrolled in this course is able to work independently on a comprehensive research paper, requiring extensive investigation and producing original research. 3 hours. As needed.
PSCI 4923 - Political Science Internship

Prerequisites: Senior standing and instructor permission.
This course provides a structured field experience in politics, government, and public policy. Students will be placed as interns with public agencies, political campaigns, or in private organizations interested in shaping public policy. Students will be required to complete assignments integrating scholarship with this practical experience. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
PSYC 2003 - General Psychology

Introduces the fundamental concepts and basic factual content of psychology Students should gain a better understanding of their own behavior and that of other people. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
ACTS Course Equivalent: PSYC 1103
PSYC 3013 - Educational Psychology

Prerequisites: Junior standing.
A survey course designed to meet the needs of prospective teachers by bringing an application of psychological principles of learning to the instructional settings. 3 hours. Fall.
PSYC 3093 - Physiological and Comparative Psychology

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 .
A study of the comparative aspects of animal and human physiology and behavior, including the nervous system, sensory systems, endocrinology, and other topics. 3 hours. Fall.
PSYC 3123 - Child Psychology

A study of the physical and mental growth of the child from infancy to adolescence. Special emphasis is placed on the social, emotional, motor development, interests, and imaginative activities of the child. Development of children in various cultural environments is explored. 3 hours. Spring.
PSYC 3153 - Research Methods

Prerequisites: PSYC 3183 .
A study of statistical methods, basic experimental procedures and designs, laboratory apparatus, and the treatment of experimental data. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as SOC 3153 .
PSYC 3183 - Statistics

Prerequisites: MATH 1023 or MATH 1053 .
Descriptive and elementary analytical statistics, their concepts, and their application. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer. Same as CRJU 3183 , SOC 3183 , and SWK 3183 .
PSYC 3191 - Advanced Topics for Individual Study
Individuals will study advanced topics in psychology and the social sciences as selected by faculty members. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
PSYC 3223 - Developmental Psychology

A comprehensive survey of human growth, maturation, and development over the lifespan. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
ACTS Course Equivalent: PSYC 2103
PSYC 3303 - Cognitive Science
An introduction to the conceptual bases of cognitive science, including topics from psychology, linguistics, ethology, and artificial intelligence. 3 hours. Spring.
PSYC 4003 - Domestic Violence

Examination of the causes, effects and legal aspects of domestic violence. Intervention techniques and prevention programs will also be studied. 3 hours. Summer. Same as CRJU 4003 , SOC 4003 , and SWK 4003 .
PSYC 4013 - Psychological Measurement

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 and PSYC 3183 .
A study of the principles of psychological measurement and their application in tests of intelligence, special aptitudes, personality, attitudes, and interests. 3 hours. Spring.
PSYC 4023 - Industrial and Organizational Psychology
A consideration of the application of psychology to such areas as personnel work, human engineering, motivation, job satisfaction, leadership, and organizational structure. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
PSYC 4033 - Abnormal Psychology

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 .
A description and explanation of the varieties of mental abnormalities: psychotic, neurotic, affective, and personality disorders, and minor maladjustmens. Includes discussion of the causes, methods of treatment, and approaches to preventing psychological maladjustments. 3 hours. Fall.
PSYC 4043 - History and Systems of Psychology

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 .
A study of the historical foundations of and the unifying principles and theories in modern psychology. 3 hours. Spring.
PSYC 4053 - Theories of Personality

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 .
A study of the personality theories of Freud, Jung, Murray, Allport, Rogers, and others. 3 hours. Spring.
PSYC 4063 - Social Psychology

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 and junior standing.
A study of how the thought, feeling, and behavior of individuals are influenced by the actual, imagined, or implied presence of others. 3 hours. Spring. Same as SOC 4063 .
PSYC 4073 - Learning

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 .
A study of the principles and problems of learning with consideration of major empirical findings and their theoretical interpretations. 3 hours. Fall.
PSYC 4083 - Adolescent Psychology

A study of the physical and mental growth of youth from emerging adolescence (middle school) through adolescence (high school) and the transition from childhood to adulthood. Effective learning and teaching strategies for the adolescent are emphasized. 3 hours. Fall.
PSYC 4093 - Career Planning in Psychology

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 or instructor permission.
Introduces students to the world of psychology beyond the classroom. Students meet guest speakers who have completed a degree in psychology and who are currently employed in various occupations. Additionally, students learn interview skills, how to write a resume, and how to apply to graduate school. 3 hours. Fall.
PSYC 4113 - Advanced Topics in Psychology
Advanced topics in psychology as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
PSYC 4213 - Advanced Topics in Psychology
Advanced topics in psychology as chosen by the faculty. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
PSYC 4133 - Introduction to Counseling Theories

Prerequisites: PSYC 2003 .
This course focuses on the study of counseling theories of Freud, Rogers, Beck, and others. This course also introduces students to basic ethical principles related to counseling and will aid the student in learning about the counselor/client relationship. Additionally, this course will include an introduction to counseling skills. 3 hours. Spring.
PSYC 4163 - Child Psychopathology

This advanced level course focuses on the etiology, classification, and treatment of the child and adolescent psychological disorders that are most frequently encountered by professionals in mental health and educational settings. 3 hours. Spring. Same as SWK 4163 .
PSYC 4173 - Criminal Profiling
Introduces students to the characteristics of serious criminals and to the proper investigation procedures to solve their crimes. 3 hours. Fall, even years. Same as CRJU 4173 .
PSYC 4191 - Advanced Topics for Individual Study
Individuals will study advanced topics in psychology and the social sciences as selected by faculty members. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
PSYC 4873 - Advanced Research Methods

Prerequisites: PSYC 3153
This course allows students to pursue a research project under the supervision of a faculty member. Projects may be derived from previous coursework, but must be substantially different. Students work independently and meet as a group as needed The research project must be presented publicly. 3 hours. As needed.
PSYC 4883 - Field Practicum

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in ENGL 1113 and ENGL 1123 , junior standing, and instructor permission.
A structured field experience relevant to the student’s major and anticipated occupational field, designed to give the student a representative perspective of the theory, methods, and problems in the practicum area. 3 hours. As needed.
PSYC 4893 - Field Practicum

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in ENGL 1113 and ENGL 1123 , junior standing, and instructor permission.
A structured field experience relevant to the student’s major and anticipated occupational field, designed to give the student a representative perspective of the theory, methods, and problems in the practicum area. 3 hours. As needed.
REC 3052 - Officiating Fall Sports

Prepares students to officiate competitive football, volleyball and soccer. Detailed coverage of sport rules and mechanics of officiating will be stressed. This course prepares students to take the examination administered by rating boards. 2 hours. Fall.
REC 3062 - Officiating Spring Sports

Prepares students to officiate competitive basketball, baseball and softball Detailed coverage of sport rules and mechanics of officiating will be stressed. This course prepares students to take the examination administered by rating boards. 2 hours. Spring.
REC 3613 - School and Community Recreation

A study of community, school, and industrial recreation, including its scope, function, and need in modern life. Emphasis given to individual, family, and small group opportunities and survey of recreation-sponsoring agencies and their programs. 3 hours. Fall.
REC 3623 - Psychology of Sports

Prerequisites: Junior standing; limited to students majoring in Exercise Science, Sport Management, or Physical Education and Health K-12.
The in-depth study of parameters of human behavior as related specifically to sport, including learning theories, motivational technique, personality factors, arousal, expectancy effects, group dynamics, leadership, aggression, burnout, and athletic injuries. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as SM 3623 .
REC 3633 - Sport Promotion and Financial Management

This course will provide students with theoretical foundations for effective sport promotion and management of financial issues such as sport consumerism, ticketing practices, sport sponsorship, sport licensing and e-commerce. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as SM 3633 .
REC 3663 - Leisure and Aging

A study of the aging process as related to leisure and recreation, specifically involving the aspects of the nature, functions, environment and resources as related to recreational and leisure opportunities for elderly citizens. 3 hours.
REC 4003 - Facility and Event Management
Survey of development, organization, and management of sport facilities and sporting events, with a focus on meeting program needs and challenges. 3 hours. Fall. Same as SM 4003 .
REC 4013 - Legal and Ethical Issues in Sports
A course designed to acquaint the undergraduate major with legal and ethical parameters and expand students’ understanding of sport law issues. 3 hours. Fall. Same as SM 4013 .
REC 4652 - Recreation Practicum I

Prerequisites: Junior standing or instructor permission.
A course devoted to providing opportunities for the student to gain practical experience in leisure programming. Experience in directing activities of participants through work in an approved area agency. 2 hours. Fall, spring.
REC 4663 - Recreation Practicum II

Prerequisites: Junior standing or instructor permission.
A course devoted to providing opportunities for the student to gain practical experience in leisure programming. Experience in directing activities of participants through work in an approved area agency. 3 hours. As needed.
REC 4676 - Recreation Internship

Prerequisites: REC 4652 and senior standing.
This course provides an internship experience for the student in an approved area agency. The experience will be specific to student needs in terms of their professional goals. The Recreation Internship Handbook provides specific information and requirements for the completion of this course. 6 hours. Fall, spring.
RUSS 1003 - Modern Russian I
An introductory course in contemporary Russian concentrating on speaking proficiency. 3 hours. As needed.
RUSS 1013 - Modern Russian II

Prerequisites: RUSS 1003 .
A continuation course in contemporary Russian concentrating on speaking proficiency. 3 hours. As needed.
RUSS 2003 - Russian Studies I
A course of directed readings on contemporary Russia associated with a month’s residence in Moscow. 3 hours. As needed.
RUSS 3003 - Russian Studies II

Prerequisites: RUSS 2003 .
A course of independent studies on contemporary Russia associated with a month’s residence in Moscow. 3 hours. As needed.
S ED 3003 - The Secondary and Middle School Curricula

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
A study of concepts and theories of the development of secondary and middle school curricula in a multi-cultural society. The focus will include the roles of various groups in curriculum planning, the social and cultural factors in planning, the availability and organization of knowledge, factors involved in selecting appropriate curricula designs and models, a study of exceptionalities, and selection of software to utilize computers in instruction. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
S ED 3013 - Methods and Materials in Secondary and Middle School English and Speech

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Corequisites: S ED 4023 .
Special materials, software, and techniques for the teaching of English and speech. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
S ED 3113 - Methods and Materials in Secondary and Middle School Mathematics and Sciences

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Candidates will apply theory and practice for teaching in an integrated curriculum classroom setting. Candidates will explore best practices for teaching and high-quality instructional material as it relates to implementing and evaluating curriculum and instruction in the classroom. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
S ED 3313 - Methods and Materials in Secondary and Middle School Social Studies

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Corequisites: S ED 4023 .
Special materials and techniques for the teaching of social studies. 3 hours. Fall.
S ED 4006 - Student Teaching in the Secondary School I

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Fifteen-week experience. Students may be assigned to the grade level of their programs of study, or a combination of grade levels if seeking K-12 licensure. The candidates’ culminating experiences involve developing and delivering comprehensive unit plans, including the associated assignments that provide evidence of their impact on all learners taught within the demonstration units. 6 hours. Fall, spring.
S ED 4023 - Residency I

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Corequisites: S ED 3013 and S ED 3313 .
The first residency semester requires experience in a classroom setting in the certification area sought under the supervision of University faculty. The candidate will be responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating instruction in collaboration with the mentor teacher and in conjunction with the SAU site coordinator. Co-teaching is required. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
S ED 4103 - Student Teaching in the Secondary School II

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Fifteen-week experience. Students may be assigned to the grade level of their program of study, or a combination of grade levels if seeking K-12 licensure. The candidates’ culminating experience involves developing and delivering comprehensive unit plans, including the associated assessments that provides evidence of their impact on all learners taught within the demonstration units. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
S ED 4016 - Student Teaching in the Secondary School II

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Fifteen-week experience. Students may be assigned to the grade level of their program of study, or a combination of grade levels if seeking K-12 licensure. The candidates’ culminating experience involves developing and delivering comprehensive unit plans, including the associated assessments that provides evidence of their impact on all learners taught within the demonstration units. 6 hours. Fall, spring.
SCI 3003 - Geographic Information Systems for the Sciences

Prerequisites: MATH 1023 or higher.
Geographic information systems (GIS) use computers to capture, store, retrieve, analyze, manipulate and display spatial data. This course introduces students to GIS, with an emphasis on environmental applications. A hands-on approach is taken, and the majority of the course is devoted to developing skills in using GIS to solve biogeoscience, environmental, and agriculture problems. Includes image processing, cartographic modeling, map algebra, multi-criteria evaluation, multiple regression, and biogeostatistics. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
SCI 3101 - Pre-Health Colloquium

An introduction to the various careers in the pre-health field. Students will learn how to be successful in preparing for careers in the various pre-health fields including, but not limited to, medicine, physician assistant, veterinary, laboratory tech, medical tech, physical therapy, occupational therapy, pharmacy, among others. hours. Fall, spring. Same as BIOL 3101 .
SCM 3033 - Supply Chain Management Technology

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business.
Supply chain management is an essential part of a firm’s strategy to gain competitive advantage. New innovations in technology, processes, and software are rapidly transforming the way firms use information to create a coordinated supply chain, make supply chain decisions, and execute these decisions effectively. This course will examine these innovations and how they are transforming the methods and effectiveness of supply chain management in the global economy. 3 hours.
SCM 3043 - Business Analytics

Prerequisites: GBUS 3183 , IS 3053 , and admission to the College of Business.
This course provides an introduction to the field of business analytics, which has been defined as the extensive use of data, statistical and quantitative analysis, exploratory and predictive models, and fact-based management to drive decisions and actions. The course uses various software systems to aid in data analysis. 3 hours. Spring. Same as IS 3043 and MKTG 3043 .
SCM 3053 - Project Management

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business.
The course covers key components of project management, including project organization, project definition, project time and cost management, project duration, outsourcing, monitoring progress, project closure, project management software, and risk management. 3 hours. Spring.
SCM 3983 - Business Internship in Supply Chain Management

Prerequisites: Junior standing and approval of the Business Internship Committee.
A structured field experience relevant to supply chain management. Each internship is designed to provide a representative and meaningful learning experience for the participating student. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
SCM 4073 - Supply Chain Management

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business.
A senior level course for marketing and management majors. The course reflects the importance of supply chains and channels of distribution in today’s business environment. 3 hours. Spring.
SCM 4053 - Environmentally Sustainable Practices

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business.
This course examines the best practices in the supply chain management (SCM) area. It emphasizes environmental sustainability as a strategic imperative in building SCM best practices, and explores the role of information technology in enabling the practices to remain sustainable from an environmental perspective. Investigating the impact of bad practices and measuring the success of good practices will also be included. 3 hours. Spring.
SM 2003 - Introduction to Sport Management

This course is designed to provide the student with information on trends, best practices, and foundational principles in sport management. The historical development of sports management, current curriculum, and career opportunities will be emphasized. 3 hours. Fall.
SM 2013 - Critical Issues in Sport Management

This course provides students with an overview of critical issues in sport management by presenting extensive discussions of past and current topics from the field. Students will learn of relevance of sociological, cultural, historical, political, psychological, and legal concepts to the management of sport; the necessary professional skills and attitudes of sport mangers; and ways in which the globalization of sport continues to affect sport management professions. 3 hours. Spring.
SM 3103 - Sport Information Management

This course is designed to provide an overview of the main components of managing information as a sport information professional. Publicity, communication channels, media relations, and electronic record keeping will be emphasized. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
SM 3313 - Sports Marketing

This course is designed to provide the student with current marketing principles as they relate to the diverse and growing field of sports, including an in-depth look at marketing practices, procedures, and operations within the wide variety of sport levels. 3 hours. Fall.
SM 3323 - Instructional Techniques in Coaching

This course examines principles and methods of instruction in the coaching profession. Communication, planning, and developing a team; player development and player evaluation will be emphasized. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
SM 3623 - Psychology of Sports

Prerequisites: Junior standing; limited to students majoring in Exercise Science, Sport Management, or Physical Education and Health K-12.
The in-depth study of parameters of human behavior as related specifically to sport, including learning theories, motivational technique, personality factors, arousal, expectancy effects, group dynamics, leadership, aggression, burnout, and athletic injuries. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as REC 3623 .
SM 3633 - Sport Promotion and Financial Management

This course will provide students with theoretical foundations for effective sport promotion and management of financial issues such as sport consumerism, ticketing practices, sport sponsorship, sport licensing and e-commerce. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as REC 3633 .
SM 4003 - Facility and Event Management
Survey of development, organization, and management of sport facilities and sporting events, with a focus on meeting program needs and challenges. 3 hours. Fall. Same as REC 4003 .
SM 4013 - Legal and Ethical Issues in Sports
A course designed to acquaint the undergraduate major with legal and ethical parameters and expand students’ understanding of sport law issues. 3 hours. Fall. Same as REC 4013 .
SM 4333 - Sports Governance

This course will look at the governance structure that exists at multiple levels in both amateur and professional sports. Sports organizations that administer rules and regulations will be studied in term of their mission, structure, and function. Current policy issues and ethical questions will be explored. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
SM 4652 - Sport Management Practicum

Prerequisites: Junior standing and instructor permission.
A course devoted to providing opportunities for the student to gain practical experience in their emphasis area in sport management. Practicum site must be approved by instructor. 2 hours. Fall, spring.
SM 4676 - Sport Management Internship I

Prerequisites: SM 4652 and senior standing.
This course provides an internship experience for the student in an approved agency. The experience will be specific to student needs in terms of their professional goals. The Sport Management Internship Handbook provides specific information and requirements for the completion of this course. 6 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
SM 4686 - Sport Management Internship II

Prerequisites: SM 4652 and senior standing.
The course provides an internship experience for the student in an approved area agency. The experience will be specific to students needs in term of their professional goals. The Sport Management Internship Handbook provides specific information and requirements for the completion of the course. 6 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
SOC 1003 - Introduction to Cultural Anthropology

An introduction to cultural anthropology, the study of culture and man in all times and all places. Major topics include the concept of culture itself, man as a culture-bearing animal, and various aspects of culture such as language, social organization, economy, technology, and religion as they appear in primitive and modern societies. 3 hours. Spring. Same as ANTH 1003 .
ACTS Course Equivalent: ANTH 1013
SOC 1013 - Introduction to Africana Studies
This course will introduce students to the various disciplines that are a part of the interdisciplinary curriculum of Africana studies. 3 hours. Fall.
SOC 2003 - Introduction to Sociology

Introduces students to the scientific study of human society and human social behavior. Topics include theory, culture, socialization, social institutions, social deviance, social stratification, and others. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
ACTS Course Equivalent: SOCI 1013
SOC 3003 - Multiculturalism

An examination of the historical and contemporary perspectives surrounding the breadth of human experience. This class will emphasize the significance of recognizing and valuing each individual’s experiences, viewpoints, and perceptions. Students will explore a deeper awareness of themselves and their interactions with others, strengthening their ability to support and engage with people in meaningful ways. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as CRJU 3003 , PSYC 3003 , and SWK 3003 .
SOC 3013 - Social Problems

A sociological study of societal problems, including social discrepancies, institutional abuse of power, population and environment, social deviance, race relations, crime, and others. 3 hours. Spring, summer.
SOC 3033 - Sociology of Marriage and Family

A sociological study of marriage, family, and kinship, both cross-culturally and within American society. Additional social phenomena examined include socialization, sexuality, sex roles, mate selection, love relationships, types of marriages, marital conflict and interaction, etc. 3 hours.
SOC 3043 - Approaches to Archaeology

An introduction to physical anthropology and archaeology covering basic concepts in physical anthropology; the origins, evolution and racial development of man; basic concepts in archaeology; and the development of culture from the early Pleistocene up through the dawn of recorded history. 3 hours. As needed. Same as ANTH 3043 .
SOC 3053 - Juvenile Justice

This course is designed to educate students concerning juvenile justice issues and explores how society responds to juvenile crime. Students will evaluate programs and processes that exist in the juvenile system; the roles of the police, courts, and corrections; and prevention efforts in schools and community-based systems. Additionally, students develop an understanding of the historical roots of juvenile justice and its evolution to present-day practice. 3 hours. Spring.
SOC 3143 - The North American Indian

The archaeology, ethnology, and history of North American Indians from the time of their arrival on this continent prior to 12,500 BCE to the present century. 3 hours. As needed. Same as ANTH 3143 and HIST 3143 .
SOC 3153 - Research Methods

Prerequisites: SOC 3183 .
A study of statistical methods, basic experimental procedures and designs, laboratory apparatus, and the treatment of experimental data. 3 hours. Spring. Same as CRJU 3153 , PSYC 3153 , and SWK 3153 .
SOC 3183 - Statistics

Prerequisites: MATH 1023 or MATH 1053 .
Descriptive and elementary analytical statistics, their concepts, and their application. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer. Same as CRJU 3183 , PSYC 3183 , and SWK 3183 .
SOC 3213 - Deviant Behavior
An examination of the nature, causes, and extent of deviant behavior among legal minors, the control and treatment of delinquents, and programs for evaluation. 3 hours. Fall. Same as CRJU 3213 .
SOC 4003 - Domestic Violence

Examination of the causes, effects and legal aspects of domestic violence Intervention techniques and prevention programs will also be studied. 3 hours. Summer. Same as CRJU 4003 , PSYC 4003 , and SWK 4003 .
SOC 4043 - Sociological Theory

Prerequisites: SOC 2003 and senior standing or instructor permission.
A selected study of past and present sociological thinkers, including Comte, Marx, Weber, Durkheim, Mead, Sorokin, Mills, Merton, Becker, Berger, and others. 3 hours. As needed.
SOC 4053 - Criminology

Prerequisites: Junior standing.
A study of the nature, causes, and extent of crime, the prevention and treatment of crime, and processes of criminal justice. 3 hours. Spring. Same as CRJU 4053 .
SOC 4063 - Social Psychology

Prerequisites: Junior standing.
A study of how the thought, feeling, and behavior of individuals are influenced by the actual, imagined, or implied presence of others. 3 hours. Spring. Same as PSYC 4063 .
SOC 4073 - Social Gerontology

Prerequisites: Junior standing.
An interdisciplinary course offering the study of the lifelong aging process, the changing social context of later life, societal response to the aged, and services available. 3 hours. Fall. Same as SWK 4073 .
SOC 4133 - Advanced Topics in Sociology
A course devoted to special topics in sociology not treated in other sociology courses. 3 hours. Spring. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
SOC 4233 - Advanced Topics in Sociology
A course devoted to special topics in sociology not treated in other sociology courses. 3 hours. Spring. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
SOC 4143 - Victimology

An introduction to victimology, with special emphasis on family violence, sexual violence, child abuse, homicide, criminal justice system, victim compensation, victim rights and issues. 3 hours. Fall, odd years. Same as CRJU 4143 and PSYC 4143 .
SOC 4153 - History of Economic Thought

This course provides a survey of the development of economic theories. Particular emphasis is placed in developing an understanding of the relationships among economic thought, political science, contemporary philosophy, and sociological issues. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as ECON 4153 and PSCI 4153 .
SOC 4303 - Sociology of Work

This course is designed to offer a critical examination of work from the sociological perspective. The changing structure of work and the organization of the workplace are addressed in relation to shifts in economic and social structures. 3 hours. As needed.
SOC 4313 - Community and Identity

The goal of this course is to address the concept of community and to critically examine how current economic and social trends impact perceptions of individual and communal identity. We will be asking if there are various levels of “community,” why some smaller communities struggle so hard to remain viable, what policies or strategies create and sustain communities, and how communities adapt to cultural and ethnic change. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 1013 - Elementary Spanish I for Professions

This course varies in its topics to provide a foundation which could be applied in various professional settings such as medicine law enforcement, education, and business. This course presents students with terminology, grammar, and extensive aspects of the Spanish-speaking culture. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 1023 - Elementary Spanish II for Professions

Prerequisites: SPAN 1013 or SPAN 1053 .
A continuation of SPAN 1013 , this course varies in its topics to provide a foundation of Spanish knowledge, which could be applied in various professional settings such as medicine, law enforcement, education and business. The course presents students with terminology, grammar and extensive aspects of the Spanish-speaking culture. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 1053 - Elementary Spanish I

A functional approach to the acquisition and development of aural, oral, reading, and writing skills through the study and mastery of basic grammatical concepts. Includes regular work in the language laboratory. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
ACTS Course Equivalent: SPAN 1013
SPAN 1063 - Elementary Spanish II

Prerequisites: SPAN 1013 or SPAN 1053 .
A functional approach to the acquisition and development of aural, oral, reading, and writing skills through the study and mastery of basic grammatical concepts. Includes regular work in the language laboratory. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
ACTS Course Equivalent: SPAN 1023
SPAN 1073 - Spanish for Health Professions

This course is designed to provide a foundation of Spanish knowledge to be applied on a daily basis in the context of various medical settings. The course presents the student with health care terminology, grammar, and cultural aspects regarding the Spanish-speaking culture. This course will be taught in English and Spanish. 3 hours.
SPAN 2033 - Intermediate Spanish I

Prerequisites: SPAN 1023 , SPAN 1063 , or placement exam.
Continues with the development of both receptive and productive skills simultaneously through readings and discussions. Spanish is used in this course and reinforced with clarification in English. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
ACTS Course Equivalent: SPAN 2013
SPAN 2043 - Intermediate Spanish II

Prerequisites: SPAN 2033 or placement exam.
A continuation of SPAN 2033 which enhances the development of both receptive and productive skills simultaneously through readings and discussions. Spanish is used in this course and reinforced with clarification in English. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
ACTS Course Equivalent: SPAN 2023
SPAN 2053 - Spanish for Heritage Speakers I

Prerequisites: Placement exam.
This course is designed for heritage speakers of Spanish who can understand and converse in Spanish but need formal language instruction to better understand the structures that lie behind their intuitive knowledge of Spanish. This course develops and/or enhances all four language skills: reading, writing, speaking, and understanding, with special attention to diction, orthography, and sentence structure. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 2063 - Spanish for Heritage Speakers II

Prerequisites: SPAN 2053 or placement exam.
This course is a continuation of SPAN 2053 . The course meets the same degree requirements as SPAN 2043 . Students may not receive credit for both SPAN 2043 and SPAN 2063. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3003 - Advanced Spanish for Professions

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
This course is designed to be a variable topics course so that a specialized advanced level of Spanish language knowledge could be applied on a daily basis in the context of various professional settings. Stress is on commercial correspondence, with the student preparing applications, memoranda, resumes, contracts, business forms, banking transactions, and business letters in the Spanish language. This course is taught in Spanish and is designed for business and finance, medicine, law enforcement, and education. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3013 - Spanish Translation I

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
This is an introductory course in Spanish/English translation, covering a variety of registers: commercial advertisements; letters; literary and journalistic pieces; and legal, medical, real estate, and technical documents. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3023 - Spanish Translation II

Prerequisites: SPAN 3013 .
This advanced course in Spanish/English translation further develops students’ linguistic competence in Spanish language, culture, and grammar to enable them to make professional translations of a variety of texts. Students will translate specialized texts from such fields as finance, business, law, journalism, literature, medicine, science, marketing, and technology. Students will gain more extensive knowledge of professional aspects of translation and an advanced understanding of linguistics, vocabulary and terminology, translation theory, and the professional code of ethics. Extensive practice in translation will be provided. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3163 - Composition and Conversation

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
Written compositions aimed at developing the student’s ability to organize material in Spanish. Includes conversational practice, oral presentations on a variety of topics, and oral interviews with Spanish-speaking individuals aimed at helping the student acquire and develop facility in the spoken language. Discussion of topics of daily interest, including Spanish contributions to literature, art, music, and drama. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
SPAN 3173 - Advanced Composition and Conversation

Prerequisites: SPAN 3163 or instructor permission.
A continuation of SPAN 3163 with a primary emphasis on improving fluency. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3183 - Spanish American Literature I

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A study of representative works in prose and poetry from the pre-Colombian period through Hispanic post-modernism. Readings will include indigenous literature of the Mayas, Aztecs, and Incas; the chronicles and letters of Christopher Columbus and Hernán Cortés, and works by later writers such as Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, Ricardo Palma, José Hernández, and modernist poets José Martí, Julián del Casal, Alfonsina Storni, and Rubén Darío. Attention will be given to socio-political conditions as a major force. 3 hours. As needed. Same as ENGL 3183 .
SPAN 3193 - Spanish American Literature II

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A continuation of SPAN 3183 covering major literary movements in Latin America from the 1820s to the present. Through the study of prose and poetry, students will be exposed to the social, artistic, and historical aspects of Latin America that these works evoke. The works of such authors as Jorge Luis Borges, Laura Esquivel, Gabrial García-Márquez, Rosario Ferré, Alejo Carpentier, Carlos Fuentes, Rosario Castellanos, Mayra Santos-Febres, Luis Rafael Sánchez, and others will be examined in this course. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. Spring, odd years. Same as ENGL 3193 .
SPAN 3323 - Spanish-English Interpretation I

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
An introductory course in the art of oral translation, this class will enable students to gain a basic to intermediate level of competence in simultaneous interpretation from one language to another, i.e. listening to one language while saying the same thing in the target language. Students will learn the fundamentals of consecutive interpreting through multiple assignments and activities which may call upon them to interpret for “real” clients, such as doctors and patients in hospitals and clinics, law enforcement personnel, attorneys and judges, court case trials, community members, guest speakers, and panel discussions. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3333 - Spanish-English Interpretation II

Prerequisites: SPAN 3323 , professional experience in legal interpreting, or instructor permission.
An advanced course in Spanish-English legal interpretation, this course provides an in-depth look at the practice of court interpreting in criminal procedures, civil litigation, and immigration hearings. Linguistic and cognitive processes during interpretation will be studied and analyzed with emphasis on identifying strategies for memory, accuracy, and speed development. Intensive practice in all modes of interpretation will be conducted with authentic materials. Political and historical issues affecting the profession will be discussed and the interpreter’s code of ethics will be examined in detail. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3873 - Spanish Internship I

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A structured and supervised field experience in Spanish language and culture designed to integrate classroom theory and/or academic learning with learning in a job site, as well as to develop functional and personal skills, strengthen future professional skills, and gain a competitive edge in the job market. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3883 - Spanish Internship II

Prerequisites: SPAN 3873 .
A structured and supervised field experience in Spanish language and culture designed to integrate classroom theory and/or academic learning with learning in a job site, as well as to develop functional and personal skills, strengthen future professional skills, and gain a competitive edge in the job market. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 3973 - Hispanic Linguistics

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
Introduction to all the major branches within the field of Hispanic linguistics: phonetics and phonology; morphology; syntax and discourse analysis; semantics; historical linguistics; dialectology; and Spanish in the U.S. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
SPAN 3993 - Advanced Spanish Grammar

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A course of comprehensive and intensive study of prescriptive Spanish grammar, including most aspects of Spanish grammar, such as phonetics, phonology, morphology, orthography, pragmatics, semantics, and syntax. The focus will be on syntax, as well as on those aspects of the language that students find most problematic. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
SPAN 4513 - Spanish Civilization

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A study of the most significant aspects of the 3,000 years of Spanish history and its contribution to Western civilization. This course is designed to stimulate thought on the political and cultural issues which constitute the major themes of Spanish history. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 4623 - Spanish-American Civilization

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A study of the intellectual heritage of Spanish-American culture, beginning with the indigenous Indian cultures in the New World, and major problems that confront Latin America. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
SPAN 4813 - Spanish Literature I

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
Representative works of writers such as Cervantes, Garcilaso de la Vega, Fray Luis de León, Lope de Vega, Calderón de la Barca, and others. Includes lectures, discussions, oral and written analyses, and a term paper. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. As needed. Same as ENGL 4813 .
SPAN 4823 - Spanish Literature II

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
This course will introduce students to the major writers and literary movements of Spain from the 18th century through the 20th century. Representative works of writers such as Fray Benito Jerónimo Feijóo, Leandro Fernández de Moratín, José de Espronceda, Gustavo Adolfo Bécquer, Rosalía de Castro, Benito Pérez Galdós, Emilia Pardo Bazán, Miguel de Unamuno, Antonio Machado, José Ortega y Gasset, Federico García Lorca, Rafael Alberti, Luis Cernuda, Rosa Chacel, Ernestina de Champourcin, Concha Méndez, Camilo José Cela, Carmen Laforet, Ana María Matute and Alfonso Sastre will be studied. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. Spring, even years. Same as ENGL 4823 .
SPAN 4923 - Special Topics: Spanish Studies

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A variable topics course in Spanish-American literature, culture, language, or civilization. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 4933 - Special Topics: Spanish and American Studies

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
A variable topics course in Spanish literature, culture, language, or civilization. This course is taught in Spanish. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 4943 - Spanish Workshop

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or instructor permission.
Workshop in Spanish addressing special needs and circumstances and providing an intensive immersion experience. 3 hours. As needed.
SPAN 4993 - Contemporary Hispanic Life and Culture

Prerequisites: SPAN 2043 or consent of instructor.
A course offering practical experiences of contemporary Spanish and Spanish-American life and culture. Presentations, films, documentaries, readings, discussions, demonstrations, and dramatizations of cultural interactions. Students will learn to converse about current issues, understand the cultural mores, and function effectively within Spanish and Spanish-American society. The class is for upper-division Spanish credit. The readings will be in Spanish, and class discussions will be in English. 3 hours. As needed. Same as MCUL 4993 .
SPCH 1113 - Introduction to Public Speaking

Principles of effective speaking; emphasis on both transmission and reception of the communicative process; the speaking mechanism and delivery. 3 hours. As needed.
ACTS Course Equivalent: SPCH 1003
SPCH 3123 - Advanced Public Speaking

Prerequisites: SPCH 1113 .
Focus on enhanced preparation and delivery of major types of public addresses, as well as oral reports appropriate to group discussion and parliamentary procedure. Effective utilization of multi-media speech aids will be stressed. 3 hours. Spring, as needed.
SPCH 3413 - Argumentation and Debate

Prerequisites: SPCH 1113 .
Designed to develop advanced research techniques, critical thinking and analysis, and applied argumentation and persuasive skills. Course also includes practice for competitive debates and presentation. 3 hours. Fall, as needed.
SPED 4013 - Adapted Kinesiology

A study of individual education for typical and atypical students; basic materials, methods; and principles of a graded program of general class activities and special adaptive education and therapeutics of recreation for the disabled and handicapped. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
SPED 4003 - Special Education 101

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course is a concentrated study of individuals in P-12 grade levels with mild disabilities (learning disabilities, mild mental disabilities, behavior disorders) including theoretical, legal, and historical foundations specifically related to learner development, learning environments, curricular content knowledge, assessment, and instructional planning & strategies. This course meets the Special Education 101 requirements as outlined in the Arkansas Department of Education rules governing educator licensure. 3 hours.
SPED 4043 - Inclusive Education

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Emphasizes how to develop a positive learning environment that supports the inclusion of diverse learners and students with exceptionalities in mainstream settings. Candidates will study and apply co-teaching practices. 3 hours. Fall.
SPED 4063 - Designing Assessments for General and Special Populations

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Candidates will design and implement effective assessments for a variety of learners as well as provide focused and meaningful feedback. In addition, candidates will critically analyze data for purposes of accountability focused on improving individual and/or organizational performance. Emphasis will be placed on strategies for using assessment data to inform instructional planning for diverse learners. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
SPED 4073 - Introduction to Special Education

This course provides an overview of the characteristics of persons with disabilities. Essential issues and theories relating to special education are emphasized. An additional emphasis is placed upon legal issues in the field of special education 3 hours. Fall, spring.
SUST 1003 - Foundations of Sustainability

Using a cross-disciplinary approach, this course introduces the various aspects of sustainability, including environmental, social, and economic dimensions of sustainability. This course will explore key knowledge areas of sustainability related to theories and evidence-based practice in several critical areas. 3 hours.
SUST 4001 - Special Topics in Sustainability

A study of current issues in the field of sustainability. Selected topics will be introduced from special readings and research. The course is designed to provide the student with in-depth knowledge in various areas of sustainability. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit with different course topics.
SUST 4002 - Special Topics in Sustainability

A study of current issues in the field of sustainability. Selected topics will be introduced from special readings and research. The course is designed to provide the student with in-depth knowledge in various areas of sustainability. 2 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit with different course topics.
SUST 4003 - Special Topics in Sustainability

A study of current issues in the field of sustainability. Selected topics will be introduced from special readings and research. The course is designed to provide the student with in-depth knowledge in various areas of sustainability. 3 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit with different course topics.
SUST 4013 - Sustainability Research and Applications

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business.
This capstone course for the sustainability minor allows students to engage in a project or research related to an area of sustainability of personal interest to them. Students will select a topic or project and then work individually or in teams to make an impact by gathering and sharing knowledge or engaging in community activities. 3 hours.
SWK 2043 - Introduction to Social Work

Generalist social work practice with application in a variety of settings. Provides, in order: an introduction to social welfare and the development of social work as a profession; the knowledge, value, and skill base of social work; special populations and concerns in social work; and completion of 30 volunteer hours at an approved site. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
SWK 2053 - Community Service-Learning Experience

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
Designed to provide an overview of the practice of social work through a service project and traditional classroom-based methods. Offered to prospective social work majors. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 3003 - Multiculturalism

An examination of the historical and contemporary perspectives surrounding the breadth of human experience. This class will emphasize the significance of recognizing and valuing each individual’s experiences, viewpoints, and perceptions. Students will explore a deeper awareness of themselves and their interactions with others, strengthening their ability to support and engage with people in meaningful ways. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as CRJU 3003 , PSYC 3003 , and SOC 3003 .
SWK 3023 - Human Behavior in the Social Environment I

Prerequisites: SWK 2043 .
Theories and knowledge of human biological, psychological, and social processes as viewed from the micro- and mezzo-level perspectives with an emphasis on individual and family development. 3 hours. Fall.
SWK 3033 - Human Behavior in the Social Environment II

Prerequisites: SWK 2043 .
Theories and knowledge of human biological, psychological, and social processes as viewed from the mezzo- and macro-level perspectives with an emphasis on group and community development. 3 hours. Spring.
SWK 3063 - Rural Social Work

Prerequisites: SWK 2043 .
A focus on the understanding of the unique dynamics, needs and problems of the rural community. An examination of interventions and policy considerations in the practice of social work in rural settings. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 3113 - Social Policy

Prerequisites: PSCI 2003.
Corequisites: SOC 3013 and SWK 2043 (can be taken as prerequisite or corequisite).
An examination of the purpose, development, and implementation of social policy The relationships between social policy, ethics, and the goals of the social work profession are examined 3 hours. Fall.
SWK 3123 - Social Work Practice I

Prerequisites: BIOL 1043 , BIOL 1041 , PSYC 2003 , SOC 2003 , and SWK 3023 .
Corequisites: SWK 3003 .
An emphasis on basic social work skills, including knowledge and techniques in interviewing and establishing the helping relationship; understanding the application of the problem-solving process; and social work as practiced in an agency setting. This course is available to social work majors only. 3 hours. Spring.
SWK 3133 - Ethics

Prerequisites: SWK 2043 .
This course examines the methods used by the social workers when advocating for individuals, groups, and communities. Special attention is given to the role of ethics in advocacy. Both case and cause advocacy are considered. 3 hours. Spring.
SWK 3143 - Child Maltreatment Theory

A focus on the understanding of theories and research in child maltreatment and the identification of individual and systems risk of protective factors related to child maltreatment. An examination of the types of child maltreatment and their effects on the emotional, social, and intellectual development of the child. Instruction will include lecture and class discussion. Analysis of individual and systems factors in child maltreatment case studies is required. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 3153 - Research Methods

Prerequisites: SWK 3183 .
A study of statistical methods, basic experimental procedures and designs, laboratory apparatus, and the treatment of experimental data. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as PSYC 3153 and SOC 3153 .
SWK 3183 - Statistics

Prerequisites: MATH 1023 or MATH 1053 .
Descriptive and elementary analytical statistics, their concepts, and their application. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer. Same as CRJU 3183 , PSYC 3183 and SOC 3183 .
SWK 3203 - Crisis Intervention:
Designed to provide guidelines of intervention in order to promote self-growth and self-realization. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 4003 - Domestic Violence

Examination of the causes, effects and legal aspects of domestic violence. Intervention techniques and prevention programs will also be studied. 3 hours. Summer. Same as CRJU 4003 , PSYC 4003 and SOC 4003 .
SWK 4053 - Critical Issues in Social Work
Introduces students to critical social work issues and to their impact upon individuals, families and communities. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 4073 - Social Gerontology

Prerequisites: SOC 2003 or SWK 2043 and junior standing.
An interdisciplinary course offering the study of the lifelong aging process, the changing social context of later life, societal response to the aged, and services available. 3 hours. Fall. Same as SOC 4073 .
SWK 4083 - Family-Centered Child Welfare

Prerequisites: SWK 2043 .
Introduction to the concepts of family preservation, risk/safety assessment, and case management with emphasis on intervention strategies and services provided through child welfare agencies and related policy issues. 3 hours. Fall.
SWK 4093 - Grant Writing

This course is designed to provide the student with a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the grant writing process. Emphasis will be placed upon how to secure federal, state, and private funds for elementary and secondary education programs, including counseling related programs. The course will address the basic components and supporting topics needed to prepare a grant application that can be successful in a funding competition. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 4121 - Social Work Field Practicum Seminar I

Corequisites: SWK 4844 .
This course will focus on issues directly involved in working with agency staff, individuals, families, groups, collaborations, teams, and other disciplines. Outside readings and internet searches focusing on the designated topics will be assigned weekly to prepare for the following week’s discussion.Experiential exercises designed to facilitate self-growth and awareness of students will focus on using various tools and techniques compatible with topics. An in-depth case presentation from the field will be required. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
SWK 4123 - Social Work Practice II

Prerequisites: SWK 3033 , SWK 3113 , and SWK 3123 .
A study of the skills needed in assessment, planning, contracting, and evaluating in the generalist model. Each skill is related to the need for professional documentation along with ethical and legal considerations. 3 hours. Fall.
SWK 4141 - Senior Seminar

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
A weekly seminar to assist the senior student in transitioning from the student role to the professional role with an exploration of some of the possible difficulties. Issues such as obtaining employment, ethics, burnout, and establishing a support network will be covered. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
SWK 4163 - Child Psychopathology

This advanced level course focuses on the etiology, classification, and treatment of the child and adolescent psychological disorders that are most frequently encountered by professionals in mental health and educational settings. 3 hours. Spring. Same as PSYC 4163 .
SWK 4173 - Advanced Topics in Social Work I

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
Varied topics of special interest to social work and the generalist model. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 4183 - Advanced Topics in Social Work II

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
Varied topics of special interest to social work and the generalist model. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 4221 - Social Work Field Practicum Seminar II

Prerequisites: SWK 4121 and SWK 4844 .
Corequisites: SWK 4854 .
This course will focus on issues directly involved in working with agency staff, individuals, families, groups, collaborations, teams, and other disciplines. Outside readings and internet searches focusing on the designated topics will be assigned weekly to prepare for the following week’s discussion. Experiential exercises designed to facilitate self-growth and awareness of students will focus on using various tools and techniques compatible with topics. An in-depth case presentation from the field will be required. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
SWK 4223 - Social Work Practice III

Prerequisites: SWK 3123 and SWK 4123 .
Corequisites: SWK 4844 or SWK 4854 .
This course is an examination of problems confronting geographic communities and the techniques social workers employ to address such problems. Various communities are considered in the practice content with an emphasis on the rural mezzo and macro practice. 3 hours. Spring.
SWK 4844 - Social Work Field Practicum I

Prerequisites: SWK 3123 , SWK 3133 , and admission to Social Work Field Practicum.
Corequisites: SWK 4121 .
Field study designed to provide students with an understanding of the practice of social work in varied settings and populations. This course requires placement in a public or private agency or institution and the completion of 240 hours of service to the agency or institution. Students will be given supervision as they synthesize knowledge, theory, and practice in a generalist practice model in direct social work within a social work setting. SWK 4844 should be taken during the semester immediately prior to SWK 4854 . 4 hours. Fall, spring.
SWK 4854 - Social Work Field Practicum II

Prerequisites: SWK 4121 , SWK 4844 , and admission to Social Work Field Practicum.
Corequisites: SWK 4221 .
Field study designed to provide students with an understanding of the practice of social work in varied settings and populations. This course requires placement in a public or private agency or institution and the completion of 240 hours of service to the agency or institution. Students will be given supervision as they synthesize knowledge, theory, and practice in a generalist practice model in direct social work within a social work setting. SWK 4854 should be taken during the semester immediately following SWK 4844 . 4 hours. Fall, spring.
TEDU 2003 - Introduction to Education

This course is designed with the intent to prepare candidates to become prospective Arkansas teachers. Candidates in this course will study the foundations of American education, including important historical moments and acts, professional behavior, student needs and diversity, instructional methods including K-12 learners health awareness, communication strategies for all stakeholders, and reflective practices to support learning. Candidates will collaborate with an Arkansas teacher to actively participate in at least 25 hours of classroom observations and field experience opportunities. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
TEDU 3013 - Creating Environments for Learning

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course will focus on increased proficiency in social-emotional learning practices and strategies for creating positive learning environments. Candidates will be provided with an understanding of the factors influencing individual and group behavior in school settings; methods of diagnosing school and classroom factors that may be eliciting the problem; and the options available for influencing student behaviors. Emphasizes classroom design including classroom procedures and expectations, organization of materials, and classroom space for optimum learner benefit. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
TEDU 3243 - STEM Content for Teachers

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Candidates will strengthen their subject matter knowledge in order to be better equipped for reaching the scientific pedagogy for K-6 students (including special needs and ESL learners). Candidates will utilize scientific inquiry along with the 5E model of teaching and the problem-based learning approach to enhance students’ critical thinking. Throughout the course, candidates will design instruction and utilize scientific technologies to effectively move student thinking toward meaningful understanding of the disciplinary core ideas; science and engineering practices; and crosscutting concepts within the realm of Earth, life, physical, space, and engineering science. 3 hours.
TEDU 4001 - Professional Learning I

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
The course will explore teaching practices based on student and candidate evaluation data during TEDU 4006 . There will be a focus on responsive and collaborative communication in the classroom. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
TEDU 4006 - Residency I

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
The first residency semester requires experience in a classroom setting in the certification area sought under the supervision of University faculty. The candidate will be responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating instruction in collaboration with the mentor teacher and in conjunction with the SAU site coordinator. Co-teaching is required. 6 hours. Fall, spring.
TEDU 4011 - Professional Learning II

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
The course will explore teaching practices based on student and candidate evaluation data during TEDU 4016 . There will be a focus on professional growth and lifelong learning. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
TEDU 4016 - Residency II

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
The second residency semester requires experience in a classroom setting in the certification area sought under the supervision of University faculty. The candidate will be responsible for planning, implementing, and evaluating instruction in collaboration with the mentor teacher and in conjunction with the SAU site coordinator. Co-teaching is required. 6 hours. Fall, spring.
TEDU 4093 - Collaborative Practice

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course will focus on advancing student learning through peer collaboration by collecting and analyzing student work. 3 hours.
TEDU 4103 - Holistic Pedagogy

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course will examine education from a holistic lens to reveal the need for teaching all children in the current American schooling system. Candidates will focus on how instruction is strengthened by the integration of pedagogy, learning, and best practices for all learners. Candidates will question, analyze, and evaluate key issues and connections between schooling, community, society. Federal and state laws for all teachers including laws related to learners’ rights, teacher responsibilities, and adherence to state code of ethics will also be included. 3 hours.
TEDU 4343 - Assessment-Driven STEM Instruction

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course uses an inquiry-style method of teaching STEM concepts that will develop thinking and problem-solving skills. This allows pre-service teachers to build science understanding and skills for standards that require their students to be actively engaged in science and engineering practices. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
TEDU 4363 - Social Studies for Teachers

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course includes information about teaching and assessing social studies in elementary and middle school classrooms. The content will focus on United States history, government, citizenship, geography, anthropology, sociology, world history, and economics. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
TEDU 4373 - Assessment-Driven Social Studies Instruction

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course focuses on the methods of instruction for social studies by discussing learners and how to foster coherent, relevant, and inclusive learning environments. Candidates will practice data-driven planning and implement high quality instruction for students. Candidates will explore professional responsibilities through reflection, feedback, collaboration, and professional learning communities. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
THDA 1002 - Ballet I

Introduction to classical ballet technique and terminology through barre and center floor work. Students will explore movement, alignment, and expression while developing an understanding of ballet’s artistic, cultural, and historical significance. The course emphasizes the connection between technical practice and broader human, social, and emotional perspectives in dance. 2 hours. Fall.
THDA 1102 - Ballet II

Prerequisites: THDA 1002 .
Continued study of classical ballet technique and terminology, building upon skills developed in Ballet I. Students refine alignment, strength, and movement quality while exploring more complex combinations, choreography, and expressive performance. The course deepens understanding of ballet’s artistic, cultural, and historical contexts and emphasizes the integration of technical skill with musicality and emotional expression. 2 hours. Spring.
THDA 2002 - Contemporary Dance I

An introduction to modern-based contemporary movement with elements of lyrical dance. Emphasis is placed on fluidity, musicality, creative expression, and the mind-body connection through technical exercises, floor work, improvisation, and across-the-floor progressions, supporting the development of strength, versatility, confidence, and individual artistic voice. 2 hours. Fall.
THDA 2102 - Contemporary Dance II

Prerequisites: THDA 2002 .
A continuation of modern-based contemporary movement with elements of lyrical dance. Emphasis is placed on balancing freedom and control while expanding technical foundations through advanced floor work, release technique, momentum-based movement, and complex across-the-floor combinations. Students further develop strength, flexibility, spatial awareness, musicality, and refined artistic expression. 2 hours. Spring.
THDA 3002 - Jazz Dance I

An introduction to the fundamentals of the Luigi and Giordano techniques of jazz dance, including warm-ups, basic technique, strength, flexibility, and mind-body connection, with an emphasis on musicality, style, and expressive performance. 2 hours. Fall.
THDA 3102 - Jazz Dance II

Prerequisites: THDA 3002 .
Expanding on the skills from Jazz Dance I, students will explore a variety of jazz styles, including commercial jazz and jazz funk, while developing choreography skills and expressive performance. 2 hours. Spring.
THDA 4002 - Musical Theatre Dance I

An introduction to original Broadway choreography, exploring the styles of Bob Fosse, Jerome Robbins, and Michael Bennett. Students will develop technical, collaborative, and performance skills essential for a career in musical theatre dance. 2 hours. Fall.
THDA 4102 - Musical Theatre Dance II

Prerequisites: THDA 4002 .
Expanding on skills from Musical Theatre Dance I, students will continue studying the styles and choreography of renowned Broadway choreographers, further developing the technical, collaborative, and performance skills essential for a career in musical theatre dance. 2 hours. Spring.
THEA 1000 - Production Run Crew

Hands-on participation in live theatre production, focused on theatre design and technology. Students will work directly with scenery, lighting, costumes, sound, media, and related equipment while supporting SAU Theatre’s annual season. Required for all SAU Theatre majors during their first two semesters of study. 0 hours. Fall, spring.
THEA 1013 - Acting I

An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through the fundamental principles and tools of performance. Students will engage with basic theatre terminology, script analysis, and character work through discovering and creating theatrical practices. 3 hours. Fall.
THEA 1101 - Theatre Dance
THEA 2101 - Theatre Dance
THEA 3101 - Theatre Dance
THEA 4101 - Theatre Dance
THEA 2301 - Theatre Production Practicum
GSTD 1002 - Freshman Seminar

This course provides an overview of the University community and resources, as well as an introduction to skills and strategies - such as time management, study, and test-taking strategies - for enhancing academic success. Required in the first regular semester of enrollment of all beginning freshmen and of all transfer students who have fewer than 24 semester credit hours. 2 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
CRJU 3023 - Criminal Evidence and Procedures

Prerequisites: CRJU 2003 or CRJU 2013 .
A study of the legal and scientific principles involved in the acquisition, preservation, analysis, and presentation of physical evidence. 3 hours. Spring.
CRJU 3043 - Criminal Law

Prerequisites: CRJU 2003 .
An examination of the administration of criminal law in the investigation, prosecution, adjudication, and sentencing of criminals. 3 hours. Fall.
CRJU 3103 - Ethics in Criminal Justice

This course will focus on ethical conduct and challenges faced by practitioners in various areas of the criminal justice system including courts, corrections, and policing Special attention will be given to recognizing and analyzing moral behavior, social moral norms, theories, and ethical behavior. Special attention will be given to identifying agency interventions designed to maintain high ethical standards in criminal justice. 3 hours. Spring.
PSCI 2003 - American Government: National

A survey of the American National Government, including the Constitution; structure and operation of the Presidency, Congress, and Judiciary; federalism; civil liberties; and politics in action. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.

Laboratory to accompany BIOL 3903 . Introduction to the methodology and techniques of human genetics. Cannot be counted toward upper-level science electives. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Fall.
BIOL 3903 - Human Genetics

Corequisites: BIOL 3901 .
This course in intended for non-biology majors and is an introduction to the principles of genetics as applied to humans, including clinical, medical, ethical, technological, and evolutionary issues that directly affect human society. Cannot be counted toward upper-level science electives. 3 hours. Fall.
BIOL 4011 - Ecology Lab

Corequisites: BIOL 4013 .
To accompany BIOL 4013 An introduction to field methods and laboratory research approaches in ecology. 1 hours. Laboratory three hours. Fall.
BIOL 4013 - Ecology

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 1213 and BIOL 1211 .
Corequisites: BIOL 4011 .
A study of the structure and function of aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems. 3 hours. Fall.
BIOL 4031 - Developmental Biology Lab

Laboratory to accompany BIOL 4033 . 1 hours. Laboratory three hours. Fall, even years.
BIOL 4033 - Developmental Biology

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 1213 , BIOL 1211 , BIOL 3033 , and BIOL 3031 .
Corequisites: BIOL 4031 .
This course will provide an in-depth study of how animals grow from embryo to adult stages, examining development at the cellular, molecular, and anatomic levels. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
BIOL 4041 - Immunology Lab

Corequisites: BIOL 4043 .
This course teaches students immunological techniques, including cell culture, immune stimulation, Western blotting, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence and ELISA. 1 hours.
BIOL 4043 - Immunology

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 3033 and BIOL 3031 .
Corequisites: BIOL 4041 .
An introduction to the cells of the immune system, immune activation, immune development, immune regulation, immune defense, and immune disorders 3 hours. As needed.
BIOL 4061 - Wildlife Ecology and Management Lab

Corequisites: BIOL 4063 .
A laboratory designed to familiarize students with current techniques and applications in wildlife management ecology. 1 hours. Spring, odd years.
BIOL 4063 - Wildlife Ecology & Management

Prerequisites: BIOL 4013 and BIOL 4011 .
Corequisites: BIOL 4061 .
An advanced course that investigates ecological models used in wildlife management. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
BIOL 4101 - Biology Colloquium

Prerequisites: Senior standing.
Discussion, preparation, and presentation of papers on current topics in biology. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
BIOL 4243 - Viral Genetics

Prerequisites: BIOL 3033 and BIOL 3031 .
An introduction to the molecular-genetic processes that underlie viral infection in all forms of cellular life. This is an upper level genetics class, so BIOL 4503 Molecular Biology is recommended as a prerequisite. 3 hours. As needed.
BIOL 4244 - Advanced Microscopy and Histology

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 1213 and BIOL 1211 .
This course will provide a general survey of microscopy techniques and sample preparation. We will cover the basic microscope structure, function, and use of light and electron microscopes. We will also cover sample preparation and mounting as well as selecting appropriate staining techniques. A major focus of this class will be practical microscope selection and use as well as acquiring and analyzing data to meet research goals. 4 hours. As needed.
BIOL 4501 - Molecular Biology Lab

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 3033 and BIOL 3031 .
Corequisites: BIOL 4503 .
Laboratory to accompany BIOL 4503 . Introduction to the techniques and methods used in the molecular biology lab, including DNA extraction, PCR, gel electrophoresis, restriction digestion, genetic transformation, RNA interference, DNA sequencing and bioinformatics analysis. 1 hours. Laboratory two hours. Spring.
BIOL 4503 - Molecular Biology

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 3033 and BIOL 3031 .
Corequisites: BIOL 4501 .
This course presents an overview of the principles of molecular biology, genome function and gene regulation with an evolutionary perspective on both the diversity and commonalities of molecular processes across major groups of life. 3 hours. Spring.
BIOL 4663 - Natural Resource Policy and Administration

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 1213 and BIOL 1211 .
Factors in evolution, range, wildlife and related natural resources administration and policies in the United States; policy components; policy formation in implementation, administration and change processes; introduction to criteria for evaluating effectiveness of policies and administration. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.

Repeatable for credit.

Student will conduct an independent research project under the guidance of a biology faculty member.
