THEA 2003 - Theatre Appreciation

A general overview of the art, history, and production techniques of theatre. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
ACTS Course Equivalent: DRAM 1003
THEA 2013 - Movement for Actors

An introduction to movement training for the stage, this course integrates anatomy, movement theory, and performance practice. Grounded in Laban Movement Analysis and Suzuki-based training, students will develop efficient, expressive movement and heightened body awareness. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 2023 - Acting II

Prerequisites: THEA 1013 .
An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through discovery of how actors collaborate. Students will develop skills in imagination, communication, and collaboration with their fellow theatre practitioners and are introduced to the craft of creating a one-person show. 3 hours. Spring.
THEA 2033 - Voice for Actors

A foundational voice training course for performance, integrating anatomy, vocal theory, and embodied practice. Drawing from the work of Fitzmaurice, Knight-Thompson, Lessac, Linklater, and Rodenburg, students will develop efficient, expressive, and sustainable vocal production. Emphasis is placed on breath, resonance, articulation, clarity, and neutral speech to cultivate the voice as a responsive and expressive instrument. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 2103 - Acting III

Prerequisites: THEA 2023 .
An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through theatrical movement practices and monologue work. Students will expand intellectual, physical, emotional, and ritual understanding of what personalization is and how it applies to the text of a play. 3 hours. Fall.
THEA 2203 - Acting IV

Prerequisites: THEA 2103 .
An exploration of the discipline and art of acting through audition preparation for theatre companies. Students will prepare self-tapes, broaden their career readiness, and investigate complex scene work. 3 hours. Spring.
THEA 2503 - Fundamentals of Design

Prerequisites: THEA 2613
A foundational theatre design course building on the concepts taught in Stagecraft. Students will explore the basics of all design specialties, including the tools, processes, and analysis methods used in professional practice, preparing them for advanced study in specific areas. 3 hours. Fall.
THEA 2513 - Costume Design

Prerequisites: THEA 2503
A practical introduction to costume design where students will develop skills in research, sketching, rendering, and fabric selection. Students will create and present design concepts, analyze construction techniques, and practice professional-level costume documentation and collaboration. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
THEA 2603 - Improvisation

An introduction to improvisation focused on spontaneity, collaboration, and ensemble storytelling. Through structured exercises, games, and scene work, students will develop active listening, adaptability, and truthful responses in unscripted performance. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
THEA 2606 - Summer Theatre Workshop
An in-depth study of theatre through the production of major plays for public presentation. 6 hours. Summer, as needed.
THEA 4606 - Summer Theatre Workshop
An in-depth study of theatre through the production of major plays for public presentation. 6 hours. Summer, as needed.
THEA 2613 - Stagecraft

An introduction to technical theatre where students gain hands-on experience with the fundamental skills of all production departments. Emphasis is placed on safety, basic tools, and collaborative work. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
THEA 2633 - Fundamentals of Acting

An introduction to practical acting skills for non-theatre majors. Students will develop confidence, imagination, concentration, and physical and vocal awareness through in-class exercises and scene work. This course will also introduce basic script and character analysis tools. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
THEA 3403 - Playwriting I

Prerequisites: THEA 3763 .
A practical introduction to playwriting where students will develop skills in crafting material for the stage. The course emphasizes dramatic structure, writing for performance, and understanding the technical limitations of theatrical production. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
THEA 3413 - Acting for the Camera

Prerequisites: THEA 2633 .
An introduction to the skills and techniques specific to acting on camera. Students will explore professional terminology, on-camera practices, and practical exercises to build confidence and adaptability for film and digital performance. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
THEA 3423 - Accents and Dialects

Prerequisites: THEA 2203 .
A voice course where students will study and practice industry-standard accents and dialects using a systematic approach and the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA). Emphasis is placed on clarity, vocal flexibility, physical and emotional connection, and effective communication in performance. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
THEA 3433 - Musical Theatre History

An overview of the development of musical theatre from the nineteenth century to present-day Broadway. Students examine key composers, lyricists, directors, choreographers, and performers, while analyzing historical, cultural, and performance elements to evaluate and compare musicals. 3 hours. Spring.
THEA 3513 - Musical Theatre Performance I

Intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre repertoire; focused on solos and scenes from Golden Age musical theatre material (pre-1965). Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
THEA 3523 - Musical Theatre Performance II

Continued intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre repertoire; focused on solos and scenes from contemporary musical theatre (1965-present). Students will also explore the process of preparing a role, from character analysis to performance choices. Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
THEA 3533 - Business of Acting

Prerequisites: THEA 2203
An introduction to acting as a business and approaches to becoming a working professional in the entertainment industry. Topics include headshots, resumes, new technologies, agents, unions, interviewing, auditioning, portfolio materials, and marketing. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
THEA 3563 - Business of Design and Production

Prerequisites: THEA 2503
An introduction to professional marketing for theatre design and production students. Students learn to organize and present portfolio materials in digital, print, and media formats while exploring software tools to showcase their work effectively. 3 hours. Fall, even years
THEA 3573 - Special Topics in Theatre
Select areas of study in theatre not addressed by other theatre course offerings. May include technical, performance, history, literature, and criticism topics. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 3613 - Hair and Makeup Design

Prerequisites: THEA 2503
An introduction to theatrical hair and makeup design. Students learn tools, products, and techniques for hair styling and wigs, as well as stage makeup application, including highlight and contour, aging, and injury effects. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
THEA 3623 - Acting Styles I

This is an intensive course in classical theatre training focused on acting (including improvisation), movement (including movement theatre, clown, and historic dance), and voice. Texts might include those written by Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides, Aristophanes, Seneca, Plautus, and Terence, and moving into early modern with Calderόn, Sor Juana de la Cruz, Moliѐre, Racine, and Marivaux. 3 hours.
THEA 3633 - Acting Styles II

Prerequisites: THEA 3623 .
This course explores acting through the creation of ritual, social context/lessons, and transformational moments. The primary approach to the class involves the finding and rehearsing of scenes in the absurd and experimental genres, supplemented by readings, discussions, exercises, improvisations, and a monologue. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 3643 - Theatre History I

Survey of the development of the physical theatre, presentation means and styles, origins and characteristics of tragedy and comedy, and representative plays from different periods of major playwrights from the origins of theatre to 1600. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
THEA 3653 - Theatre History II

Survey of the development of the physical theatre, presentation means and styles, origins and characteristics of tragedy and comedy, and representative plays from different periods of major playwrights from 1600 to the present. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
THEA 3663 - Performance in Shakespeare

Prerequisites: THEA 2633 or instructor permission.
Approaches to acting the works of Shakespeare will be explored by various acting and vocal exercises. Two plays and sonnets will be explored for their action and character. Scansion of iambic pentameter, use of figures of speech, and use of verse and prose are just a few skills that will be developed. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
THEA 3673 - Creative Dramatics

Prerequisites: THEA 2023
An introduction to the process of creative and performing works for children. Students will learn about the structure and techniques of Theatre for Young Audience (TYA) plays, culminating in both in-class and out-of-class performances for live audiences. 3 hours. Fall, even years.
THEA 3763 - Script Analysis

A chronological and thematic study of dramatic literature through a wide range of plays, examined as literature intended for theatrical performance. Students will explore theatre movements, history, cultural context, structure, genre, and form as frameworks for playwrights’ work and scholarly interpretation. 3 hours. Spring.
THEA 3813 - Directed Study in Theatre I

Individually designed to meet needs of students concentrating in drama. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 3823 - Directed Study in Theatre II

Individually designed to meet needs of students concentrating in drama. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 3833 - Stage Management

An introduction to the skills needed for professional stage management. Students learn to notate cues and blocking, call performances, create rehearsal and tech schedules, and use other essential stage management tools. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
THEA 4013 - Survey of Black Theatre and Film
Students will explore the history of African American theatre from the early 19th century to the present. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 4513 - Musical Theatre Performance III

Continued intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre repertoire. Focused on contemporary commercial music audition cuts for jukebox and pop-influenced musicals. Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
THEA 4523 - Musical Theatre Performance IV

Continued intensive technique work in auditioning, acting, and musical theatre; focused on solos and scenes from the works of Stephen Sondheim. Students will also explore the process of preparing a role, from character analysis to performance choices. Significant personal and group preparation is required outside of class. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
THEA 4533 - Advanced Design Practicum I

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
Advanced study in theatre design where students will develop artistic and practical skills in their area of focus, emphasizing conceptual thinking and the collaborative design process. Students will create two projects using a Shakespeare play and a classical play. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 4563 - Advanced Design Practicum II

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
Advanced study in theatre design where students will develop artistic and practical skills in their area of focus, emphasizing conceptual thinking and the collaborative design process. Students will create two projects using a contemporary American play and a musical. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 4613 - Scenic Design

Prerequisites: THEA 2503 .
An in-depth examination of theatrical scenic design through a project-driven approach. Students will focus on the principles of design as applied to scenery, theatrical color theory, drafting, and modeling. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
THEA 4623 - Lighting and Sound Design

Prerequisites: THEA 2503 .
An in-depth examination of theatrical lighting and sound design using a project-driven approach. Instruction emphasizes color theory, equipment selection, light and sound plot development, integration with scenic structure, sound editing, and basic theatrical sound engineering. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
THEA 4633 - Directing I

Prerequisites: THEA 3763 .
An introduction to the building blocks of the director’s process with emphasis on understanding and clarifying story and dramatic action. Students will engage in script analysis, exploration of symbolic imagery, blocking and stage composition, collaboration with actors and designers, and the creation of a director’s script. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
THEA 4853 - Devised Theatre

Prerequisites: THEA 2203 .
An introductory course in devised theatre, the process of theatre creation in a collaborative manner. The ensemble will create a theatrical piece, original or adapted, with the artists working as a collective. Students will be exposed to a variety of pedagogies in ensemble theatre-making, including adaptation and found text, viewpoints and composition, improvisation, and theater for social change. Students will study earlier works of devised theater as well as the history of theater as a tool for social comment and change. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.

Structured experience in a professional or university setting other than Southern Arkansas University in performance, production, stage management, costuming, or other areas of theatre. 3 hours. As needed.
THEA 4922 - Project in Theatre

USTD 3003 - Information Literacy

Students will learn processes of locating, organizing, using, producing, and distributing information in print, electronic, and other formats in a wide variety of academic disciplines in the humanities, behavioral, and social sciences, including history, criminal justice, theater, philosophy, etc. Students will learn how information resources and collections are designed and delivered, as well as effective research strategies for the conducting research, and how to access information in a variety of print and electronic formats including databases, digital libraries, and the Internet. Students will learn how to evaluate resources for quality, including how to select and use information to accomplish a specific purpose while considering the economic, legal, ethical, and social issues relating to the use of information. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer..
USTD 3983 - Field and Leadership Experience

Students who receive unique opportunities with public or private institutions for which internships in individual academic disciplines are not available can receive course credit through this course. 3 hours. As needed.
WELD 2005 - Pipe Welding II
This course advances pipe welding skills into the materials of stainless and includes the process of TIG in the positions of 2G, 5G, and 6G. 5 hours.
WELD 2015 - High Frequency TIG & Pipeline Welding

This course focuses on key information and skills for welding with Aluminum materials using the Hi Frequency TIG method. Positions will include fillet welds in positions of 1F, 2F, and 3F per American Welding Society specification. Further, this course will give students training in the specialized process of pipeline welding (typically downhill travel). Position for this method of pipeline welding will include 5G only, per American Welding Society. 5 hours.
WELD 2025 - Welding Capstone

This course addresses the overall skill sets acquired throughout the training, allowing a collective review of GTAW and SMAW weld processes in the 2G, 5G, and 6G positions per American Welding Society specification. 5 hours.
WELD 3003 - Computer Aided Weldment Design

Students will learn how to design welded structures and frames for manufacturing purposes. Basic framework design, creating structural members from, adding gussets, caps weld beads, and stiffening plates will be covered. Students will also learn how to create weldment detailed drawings, bill of materials, and cut-list for documentation purposes. 3 hours. Spring.
WELD 3023 - Welding Metallurgy

Students will learn the material science aspect of different welding technologies. Heat flow, basic solidification process and grain structures, stress, chemical reactions in welding, and phase transformations in welding processes will be covered. 3 hours. Fall.
WELD 3043 - Welding Automation and Robotics

This course will cover the automation of the welding processes in great detail. A FANUC or a similar welding automation robot will be used in a classroom setting to demonstrate and program the automation robot. Students will be familiar with the robot coordinate system, learn how to program a robotic arm to perform welding, learn how to orient the parts, learn how to align the torch, learn how to edit the program, etc. 3 hours. Spring.
WELD 4893 - Design Projects in Welding

Students will work on projects related to welding and apply their learned knowledge from various welding technology courses. Projects will be assigned to different student groups. Submission of proposals may be required prior to the actual project work. Students will build their teamwork skills through these projects. Technical report and oral presentations may be required. 3 hours. Fall.
WELD 4932 - Advanced Topics in Welding

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
Courses devoted to special topics in welding engineering technology developing from recent trends and/or academic presentation. 2 hours. As needed.
ACCT 6003 - Accounting for Decision Making

The application of accounting to firms in manufacturing, retailing, and service industries. The course emphasizes using accounting information to make management decisions and includes analyzing financial statements, cost analysis, budgeting, and capital investment decisions. This course also covers corporate governance, accountability, and ethical decision making. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
ECON 6003 - Managerial Economics

The course focuses on the analysis of markets with concentrations on cost analysis, determinants of market demand, pricing strategy, market power, implications of government policies, and a collaborative research project using economic analysis. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
FIN 6003 - Managerial Finance

To examine and apply the theories, tools, and techniques utilized in the financial management of the firm. An emphasis is placed on developing the financial knowledge and skills necessary to make decisions in a business setting. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MGMT 6003 - Strategic Planning and Analysis

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
This course is designed to prepare students to be senior managers for the increasingly competitive business world. The emphasis of this course will be on the strategic analyses, decisions, and actions that organizations take to create sustainable competitive advantages, with the consideration of both the internal condition and the external environment, through chapters, readings, case analyses, and simulations. We will also discuss issues related to technical advancements, global conditions, ethical decision making, corporate social responsibility, stakeholder theory, and the relationship of business and government. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
MGMT 6013 - Human Behavior in Organizations

A theoretical and application-based survey of the human factors in organization management. The course gives consideration to the impact of dynamic forces like globalization and technology on the organization. The course utilizes a combination of textbook readings, exercises, and research studies of actual organizations to provide MBA students with a working knowledge of the personal and interpersonal processes involved in the management and leadership of organizations. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MGMT 6043 - Business Analytics

Statistical concepts and methodology useful in understanding, assessing, and controlling operations of business statistics. The major objectives are both an understanding of the statistical methods and the application coverage of topics including collection and presentation of data, probability theory, sampling distributions, hypothesis testing, analysis of variance, regression, and non-parametric statistics. SPSS will be highly utilized throughout the semester. In addition to understanding the basic concepts of statistics, this course will focus mainly on the applications of statistics in helping managers make better decisions. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MKTG 6023 - Strategic Marketing

The study of elements that affect managerial decisions in marketing. Emphasis is placed on analysis, planning, implementation, and control of marketing programs in a competitive environment utilizing the case method and/or computer simulations. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
SCM 6003 - Enterprise Resource Planning

This course explores the role of information technologies in business with emphasis on the study of the development and management of information systems to support the operational, administrative, and strategic needs of modern organizations. The course examines the management of supply chains from an enterprise resource perspective and emphasizes on managerial decision-making. The course also explores the benefits, issues and challenges associated with information technology usage for businesses. 3 hours. Fall.
PA 6003 - Principles of Public Administration

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course is designed to develop an understanding of the field of public administration. This involves the exploration of a variety of topics in some depth, integrating them with the objective of forming an overall perspective of the conduct of the public’s interest. Topics will include decision theory, ethics, major figures and theories of public administration, bureaucratic theory, and overview of contemporary issues. 3 hours. Fall.
PA 6053 - Public and Non-Profit Budgeting

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
Reviews theories of budgeting in the public and non-profit sectors (including the impact of macroeconomic fiscal policies). Examines budget tools (including a variety of automated budgeting systems) used to apply the theories to policy choices and to construct operating and capital budgets, to manage risk, and to assure accountability. 3 hours. Fall.
PA 6063 - Public Policy

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
Course focuses on public policy issues, decision processes, resource allocation, and understanding the political and economic nature of public policy. Will cover in depth theories of the policy process, policy formulation, and execution. Specific attention will be paid to justifications for (or against) governmental interventions. 3 hours. Fall.
PA 6073 - Research Methods

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
Emphasizes ethical methods of scientific inquiry, including quantitative and qualitative methods of analysis, and research design and implementation. Encourages critical analysis of the research underlying policy recommendations. Introduces students to a wide variety of social science research techniques and assists them in developing their own research projects. 3 hours. Spring.
PA 6083 - Organizational Leadership

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
Surveys theories and types of leadership; provides analyses of techniques for creating motivation and cohesion in complex organizations and describes design/administration of structures for successful decision-making. 3 hours. Fall.
PA 6113 - Professional Project

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The professional project is intended to be a capstone for the MPA degree. It should demonstrate a level of competence on the part of the student that is expected of one with a professional degree. This will involve providing a product for a public or non-profit agency. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer. Same as SE 6113 .
PA 6153 - Human Resources in Public Organizations

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course introduces students to the field of human resource management. It focuses on the knowledge and skills required by both personnel officers and those who manage personnel on a daily basis. 3 hours. Spring.
PA 6263 - Program Evaluation

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course is designed to develop an understanding of the theoretical underpinnings and practical applications of the evaluation of public programs. Will cover governmental and nonprofit evaluation requirements. Course will focus on stakeholder analysis, formal research design, data collection procedures, process, and impact evaluations. 3 hours. Spring.
MCIS 6123 - Decision Science

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The course introduces the concepts of decision support systems and artificial intelligence systems as components of information systems. Survey of the analysis, design, and implementation of systems for decision support, including data management systems, knowledge engineering, expert systems, and intelligent agents. 3 hours. As needed.
MCIS 6133 - User Interface Design

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This courses studies human factors of interactive software, interactive styles, design principles and considerations, development methods and tools, interface quality and evaluation methods. 3 hours. Fall.
MCIS 6153 - Software Engineering

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course focuses on the system development life cycle for creating web-based information systems analysis and design. It introduces different paradigms for developing web software, the key stages of the life cycle and identifies key deliverables for each stage. 3 hours. As needed.
MCIS 6163 - Computer Networking

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The course will cover networking from the lowest levels of data transmission and wiring to the highest levels of application software, explaining how underlying technologies provide services and how Internet applications use those services. 3 hours. As needed.
MCIS 6173 - Information and Networking Security

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will survey network-based and Internet-based security applications and standards including topics of cryptography. It covers algorithms and protocols underlying network security applications, encryption, hash functions, digital signatures, and key exchange. 3 hours. Spring.
MCIS 6283 - Machine Learning

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course covers the theoretical and practical fundamentals of machine learning. Students will explore the key concepts of machine learning in a practical approach. Students will learn various machine learning tasks including algorithms and techniques such as linear regression, logistic regression, support vector machines, reinforcement learning, Bayesian decision theory, hidden Markov models, and neural networks. 3 hours. Spring.
MCIS 6303 - Survey of Literature in Computer Science

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course focuses on methodology of survey of computer science literature including taxonomy, organization, and presentation. 3 hours. As needed.
MCIS 6913 - Thesis

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course focuses on investigating one or more research problems and reporting the findings. 3 hours. As needed.
SE 6113 - Professional Projects

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The professional project is intended to be a capstone for the MPA degree. It should demonstrate a level of competence on the part of the student that is expected of one with a professional degree. This will involve providing a product for a public or non-profit agency. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer. Same as PA 6113 .
TEDU 4002 - Professional Learning I

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
The course will explore teaching practices based on student and candidate performance data. There will be a focus on responsive and collaborative communication in the classroom. 2 hours. Fall, spring.
HPSS 4383 - Workshop in HPSS

Prerequisites: Senior standing.
Specific and selected sports, problems, issues, and trends in various areas of the HPSS discipline. 3 hours. Spring. Repeatable for credit up to 6 total credit hours.
HC 4011 - Advanced Topics in Honors

Prerequisites: HC 1013 or consent of the Honors Director.
Advanced topics related to honors education as chosen by honors faculty on campus or by honors faculty extramurally. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
HC 4012 - Advanced Topics in Honors

Prerequisites: HC 1013 or consent of the Honors Director.
Advanced topics related to honors education as chosen by honors faculty on campus or by honors faculty extramurally. 2 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
HC 3011 - Advanced Topics in Honors

Prerequisites: HC 1013 or consent of the Honors Director.
Advanced topics related to honors education as chosen by honors faculty on campus or by honors faculty extramurally. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
HC 3012 - Advanced Topics in Honors

Prerequisites: HC 1013 or consent of the Honors Director.
Advanced topics related to honors education as chosen by honors faculty on campus or by honors faculty extramurally. 2 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit up to six total credit hours with different course topics.
PSYC 3003 - Multiculturalism

An examination of the historical and contemporary perspectives surrounding the breadth of human experience. This class will emphasize the significance of recognizing and valuing each individual’s experiences, viewpoints, and perceptions. Students will explore a deeper awareness of themselves and their interactions with others, strengthening their ability to support and engage with people in meaningful ways. 3 hours. Fall, spring. Same as CRJU 3003 , SOC 3003 , and SWK 3003 .
CRJU 4063 - Field Practicum

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in CRJU 3103 .
This course is to provide advanced undergraduate students with opportunities to participate in criminal justice settings such as law enforcement, criminal court, correctional institutions, probation and parole, etc , so that they may experience first-hand how that agency operates. The program gives students practical experience by working with and observing trained professionals. Thus, students can combine classroom learning with real situations. The combined experience of the internship and classroom learning experience fills a void in the traditional curriculum for students. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
AGED 4033 - Experiential Learning in Agriculture

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Corequisites: AGED 4013 .
Planning, organizing, and implementing experiential learning opportunities in agricultural education settings such as Supervised Agricultural Experience (SAE) programs, laboratories, and school-based enterprises. 3 hours. Spring.
SWK 4153 - Death and Dying

This course will provide a Social Psychological approach in the examination of death and grieving. Students will be introduced to empirical research on death related topics from a multidisciplinary approach. This course is designed to prepare generalist practitioners with the evolution of death and dying by presenting a comprehensive review of key topics such as personal, social, cultural, legal, philosophical, spiritual, and ethical issues related to death and dying. This course specifically emphasis how to understand and cope with problems and issues that arise before, during, and after the end of life stage. 3 hours. As needed.
SWK 4171 - Advanced Topics in Individual Study

Prerequisites: Instructor permission required
Advanced study in chosen area of social work. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
PSYC 4143 - Victimology

An introduction to victimology with special emphasis on family violence, sexual violence, child abuse, homicide, criminal justice system, victim compensation, victim rights and issues. 3 hours. Fall, odd years. Same as CRJU 4143 and SOC 4143 .
AGED 4003 - Methods of Teaching Agricultural Mechanics

Prerequisites: Unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
Corequisites: AGED 4023
Planning, directing, and evaluating teaching and learning in agricultural mechanics. 3 hours. Spring.
MUED 3003 - Choral Conducting
Conducting and rehearsal techniques, performance styles, choral literature, and programming. Score study and conducting of choral and instrumental groups also included. 3 hours. As needed.
CRJU 3233 - Cyber Crime

Prerequisites: CRJU 2003
Examination of the various types of cybercrime currently threatening computer users, as well as the characteristics of the offenders and victims. 3 hours. As needed.
CRJU 4923 - Senior Project

Prerequisites: Senior standing. Instructor permission required.
A guided senior project in cyber criminology is to be completed under the supervision of an instructor. The project could include the development and study of cyber crimes, the knowledge of the current state of the law, or possible combinations. 3 hours. As needed.
BIOL 3163 - Plant Ecology

Prerequisites: Grade of C or greater in BIOL 1213 and BIOL 1211 .
Corequisites: BIOL 3161
This course will cover abiotic and biotic factors that affect plant abundance and distribution, as well as the structure and dynamics of plant populations and communities. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
BIOL 3161 - Plant Ecology Lab

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 1213 and BIOL 1211 .
Corequisites: BIOL 3163
To accompany BIOL 3163 - Plant Ecology . 1 hours. Laboratory 2 hours. Spring, odd years.
CHEG 4033 - Process Dynamics and Control

Prerequisites: CHEG 2053 .
Corequisites: MATH 3033 .
Understanding the basics of process control and operation is vital for the proper operation and the safety of chemical processes. This course provides students with the necessary knowledge on process dynamics, mathematical modeling of chemical processes, Laplace transform, transfer function models, feedback controllers, control system instrumentation, controllers tuning, dynamic behavior and stability of control systems, frequency response analysis and control system design, feedforward and ratio control, and Piping and Instrumentation Diagram. The acquired knowledge can be applied to different engineering systems involved in chemical, petrochemical, petroleum, biochemical, pharmaceutical, food, and mineral industries. 3 hours. Fall.
ENGR 2030 - Safety and Guidance

This is a non-credit course designed to provide safety and guidance training for students who will be using machine shop tools and other laboratory equipment where safety is crucial. Approval from the faculty advisor is required. Credit/No Credit. 0 hours. Fall, spring.
TEDU 4012 - Content Pedagogy in STEM

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
A content design course in which candidates will plan example learning units of study and equitable, culturally responsive opportunities for STEM students based upon their understanding of how students learn and develop mathematics and science knowledge, skills, and habits of mind. Candidates will make appropriate connections to math, science, and engineering practices and crosscutting concepts in their instructional planning content area. 2 hours.
TEDU 4353 - Assessment-Driven Math and Science Instruction

Prerequisites: Conditional or unconditional admission to the Educator Preparation Program.
This course is an inquiry style method of teaching STEM concepts that will develop the thinking and problem-solving skills pre-service teachers will need to build science and math understanding and skills for standards that require students to be actively engaged in science, technology, engineering, and math practices. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours.
MUEN 1011 - Jazz Lab
An ensemble course designed for the study and performance of beginner/intermediate jazz band literature, concepts, and skills. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
MUEN 3011 - Jazz Lab
An ensemble course designed for the study and performance of beginner/intermediate jazz band literature, concepts, and skills. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
MUEN 1111 - Jazz Combo
The study and performance of jazz music, skills, and concepts in a combo/chamber setting. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
MUEN 3111 - Jazz Combo
The study and performance of jazz music, skills, and concepts in a combo/chamber setting. 1 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
MUED 1001 - Fundamentals of Conducting

During their course of study, students will be taught the fundamentals of conducting, including the following: basic time-beating patterns; the use of non-verbal communication in the musical ensemble, foreign-language terms dealing with tempo, orchestration, articulation, notation, and form; dealing with transpositions for a variety of instruments; conducting different articulations; the role of the left hand in conducting; preparatory gestures; and the use of the baton. 1 hours.
MGMT 4101 - International Studies and Field Experience

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business and instructor permission.
An introduction to the basics of international business combined with a field experience in an international location. The instructor will emphasize culture, business environment, and practices for the country of the field experience. Students will enroll in MGMT 4102 during the semester prior to the field experience and MGMT 4101 during the international field experience. 1 hours. Spring intersession.
MGMT 4102 - International Studies and Field Experience

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business and instructor permission.
An introduction to the basics of international business combined with a field experience in an international location. The instructor will emphasize culture, business environment, and practices for the country of the field experience. Students will enroll in MGMT 4102 during the semester prior to the field experience and MGMT 4101 during the international field experience. 2 hours. Spring.
MULI 3022 - Survey of Choral Literature

This course will survey Western choral literature from the Medieval to Contemporary Periods. Class time will be dedicated to score study and group discussion informed by readings and lectures that contextualize the works. In addition to learning about significant composers from the major eras of choral literature, we will explore diverse choral genres and trace their evolution over time and across geographic regions. 2 hours. Spring, odd years.
MULI 4021 - Vocal Music Literature

This course is designed to survey the development of Western solo vocal literature from approximately 1550 to the present, with emphasis on Italian, German, French, English, and American song. Opera and oratorio literature will be discussed as it pertains to the progression of solo song, but is not the focus of this course. 1 hours. Fall, even years.
THEA 3443 - Playwriting II

Prerequisites: THEA 3403
A continuation of Playwriting I, this course deepens the study of the art and craft of dramatic writing. Students will focus on process, exploring character development, language, theatricality, metaphor, and revision, culminating in a full-length stage play. 3 hours. Spring, odd years.
THEA 4643 - Directing II

Prerequisites: THEA 4633
An exploration of the director’s process, with emphasis on clarifying story and dramatic action. Students will collaborate with playwrights and designers while developing practical skills in script analysis, use of imagery and symbolism, blocking and stage composition, and working effectively with actors. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
THEA 4921 - Project in Musical Theatre

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
Major project in musical theatre. Student will present a 30-minute showcase of their own making which represents all aspects of their musical theatre training. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
THEA 2042 - Musical Theatre Repertoire

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
A broad survey of all existing musical theatre literature and resources that will enable students to critically select their own repertoire and develop their audition book. 2 hours. Fall.
THEA 1300 - Theatre Production Practicum

Prerequisites: Instructor permission required.
A design lab course where students will create and present theatrical design work in support of SAU Theatre productions. 0 hours. Fall, spring.
THEA 1100 - Voice Studio

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
A performance lab course where students will present songs, monologues, and scenes from the theatre and musical theatre canons. 0 hours. Fall, spring. Repeatable.
THEA 1110 - Acting Studio

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
A performance lab course where students will present monologues and scenes from the theatre canon. 0 hours. Fall, spring. Repeatable.
MAT 5013 - Classroom Assessment

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
Candidates will design and implement effective assessments for a variety of learners as well as provide focused and meaningful feedback. In addition, candidates will critically analyze data for purposes of accountability focused on improving individual and/or organizational performance. Emphasis will be placed on strategies for using assessment data to inform instructional planning for diverse learners. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MAT 5023 - Survey of Exceptional Individuals

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course is a general survey of exceptional individuals from birth to 21 years, and an introduction to special education including special education history and law; disability causations; definitions and classifications systems, characteristics of all categories of exceptional learners (disabled and gifted); provision of services and appropriate educational interventions. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MAT 5083 - Creating Environments for Learning

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will focus on increased proficiency in social-emotional learning practices and strategies for creating positive learning environments. Candidates will be provided with an understanding of the factors influencing individual and group behavior in school settings, methods of diagnosing school and classroom factors that may be eliciting the problem, and the options available for influencing student behaviors. Emphasizes classroom design, including classroom procedures and expectations, organization of materials, and classroom space for optimum learner benefit. This course will require candidates to learn and practice strategies and techniques through authentic and interactive field experiences. 3 hours. As needed.
MAT 5093 - Collaborative Practices

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will focus on advancing student learning through peer collaboration by collecting and analyzing student work. Candidates will engage in professional development, community building, and reflective practice. hours. As needed.
MAT 5103 - Holistic Pedagogy

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will examine education from a sociocultural, sociopolitical, and sociohistorical lens to reveal the need for equity in the current American schooling system. Candidates will focus on strengthening instructional equity by integrating culturally responsive/sustaining pedagogy, social-emotional learning, trauma-informed pedagogy, and restorative justice practices. Candidates will question, analyze, and evaluate critical issues and connections between schooling, community, society, and policy. Federal and state laws for all teachers will also be included, including laws related to learners’ rights, teacher responsibilities, and adherence to the state code of ethics. 3 hours. As needed.
MAT 6073 - Learning Theory

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will explore a wide range of subjects in educational psychology that impact student learning, including theories of cognition and motivation, and apply them to academic work. Content will cover strategies to improve student academic performance. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MAT 5003 - Strategies for Content Area Reading

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will provide education majors with an overview of the instructional strategies for teaching and integrating reading into content areas. Students will develop a conceptual understanding of reading processes and appropriate instructional strategies, which emphasize reading skills necessary for the learning of content area information. 25 hour field experience required. 3 hours. As needed.
MAT 6083 - Reading Diagnostics

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
A course focusing on reading diagnostics in the classroom. Students will learn to identify reading difficulties in K-12 learners and will learn techniques to help the struggling reader. 25 hour field experience required. 3 hours. As needed.
MAT 5173 - Teaching Literacy I

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
An introduction to teaching reading in the elementary classroom. There will be an emphasis on the science of reading and the development, assessment, and instruction of individual and small groups of students. Requires 25 hours of field experience. 3 hours. As needed.
MAT 5273 - Teaching Literacy II

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will focus on literacy acquisition, assessment, and instruction in the K-6 classroom. This course will focus on applying foundational knowledge in the areas of phonological awareness, phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, comprehension, fluency, writing, and assessment. 25 hour field experience is required. 3 hours. As needed.
MAT 6033 - Internship I

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The supervised internship is to be completed when the candidate obtains a job in an appropriate school. The candidate is provided with supervise, on-the-job experiences. The experiences will be accompanied by online coursework and individual supervision at the school site designed to provide evaluation, reflection, and analysis of the field experiences. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MAT 6043 - Internship II

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The supervised internship is completed after Internship I. The candidate must still have a job at an appropriate school. The candidate is provided with supervised on-the-job experiences. The experiences will be accompanied by online coursework and individual supervision at the school site designed to provide evaluation, reflection, and analysis of the field experiences. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MAT 6053 - Residency I

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The candidates’ culminating experience involves developing and delivering comprehensive lessons including the associated assessments that provide evidence of the positive impact on learning. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
MAT 6063 - Residency II

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The candidates’ culminating experience involves developing and delivering comprehensive lessons, including the associated assessments that provide evidence of the positive impact on learning. 3 hours. Fall, spring.
AGRI 6063 - Advanced Leadership for Agricultural Professionals

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
Concepts and practices in planning and presenting materials to agricultural groups. Includes an in-depth study and application of leadership skills, concepts of community development, dynamics of technological change. 3 hours. Summer.
AGRI 6083 - Professional Development in Agriculture

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
Students will select an agriculture facility in Arkansas or another state and study the facility for one semester. They will interview professionals within the facility and spend at least 100 hours job shadowing employee(s). With guidance from a professor of agriculture from SAU, the student will prepare a written report and present his/her final report to the agriculture faculty and other professionals. 3 hours. Spring.
AGRI 6123 - Philosophy of Agricultural Education

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course focuses on the historical and philosophical developments in education that brought about education in agriculture. 3 hours. As needed.
AGRI 6133 - Experiential Learning

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course focuses on theory and practice in facilitating learning from experience in formal, informal, and non-formal settings. 3 hours. As needed.
AGRI 6153 - Leadership of Volunteers

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course focuses on the dynamics in agricultural education and in the life of the community. 3 hours. As needed.
EDUC 6003 - Educational Research

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course is designed to prepare the educator to be a consumer of educational research as well as how to participate as a producer of new knowledge through the research process. Appropriate research principles and methodologies to enhance teaching, student learning, and school improvement will be emphasized. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
AGRI 6143 - Adult Education in Agriculture

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course focuses on the identification of the basic principles which motivate adult learners and the procedures to implement these principles in bringing about changes in adult behavior. 3 hours. As needed.
AGRI 6163 - Practical Experiences for Career Orientation

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
A course designed to provide hands-on experience in teaching a career orientation course. The course emphasizes a variety of hands-on and observation techniques required to carry out a career orientation program. 3 hours. Summer.
AGRI 6173 - Methods of Organizing and Teaching Career Orientation

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The course will present the 16 USOE career clusters, resources available, and standards required by the State Department of Vocational and Technical Education. 3 hours. Summer.
EDUC 5033 - Classroom Assessment

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course shows in-service teachers how to use classroom testing accurately and formatively to increase their teaching effectiveness and make a difference in how well students learn. Teachers will learn clear and concise guidelines on how to develop quality classroom assessments. Particular attention is paid to the implications of testing on teaching and the increasing importance of educational assessment in an era of state standards and teacher evaluations based on students’ tests scores. 3 hours. Spring.
EDUC 6043 - Current Issues and Trends in Education

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course explores issues and trends in education, which face the region, state, and nation using historical, philosophical, political, multicultural, and other forces as a basis to study how ideas and opinions are shaped. 3 hours. Spring, summer.
EDUC 6063 - Applications of Technology in Education

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course will address uses of technology to increase productivity, enhance classroom instruction, and facilitate campus activities. 3 hours. Spring.
EDUC 6083 - Application of Learning Theories

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This is a study of the principles and problems of learning with consideration of major empirical findings and their theoretical interpretations. 3 hours. Spring, summer.
EDUC 6403 - School Law

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course is an introduction to the federal and state legal systems and applicable federal and state educational case law. Particular emphasis is placed on the current federal and state laws and regulations governing students, employees, finance, and the administration of programs for special student populations. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
BIOL 3101 - Pre-Health Colloquium

An introduction to the various careers in the pre-health field. Students will learn how to be successful in preparing for careers in the various pre-health fields including, but not limited to, medicine, physician assistant, veterinary, laboratory tech, medical tech, physical therapy, occupational therapy, pharmacy, among others. hours. Fall, spring Same as SCI 3101 .
NURS 3090 - Techniques of Health Assessment Lab

Prerequisites: Junior standing and admission to the Nursing program.
This is the lab section of NURS 3093 - Techniques of Health Assessment .
Knowledge and skills necessary to conduct a comprehensive health assessment for individuals across the life span are presented, including history taking, review of systems, and physical examination techniques. Emphasis is placed on integrating theoretical knowledge with psychomotor assessment skills to equip students for entry level practice (3 credit hours are divided into 2.5 credit hours lecture and 0.5 credit hours lab learning experiences, which is a 1:3 ratio, or 1.5 lab contact hours/week [22.5 total lab contact hours]). 0 hours. Fall, spring.
NURS 3200 - Foundations Clinical

Prerequisites: Prerequisites: Junior standing and admission to the Nursing program.
This is the clinical section of NURS 3206 - Nursing Care I: Foundations .
Essential knowledge, attitudes, and skills for professional nursing practice are presented. Principles of physical, biological, and behavioral sciences are integrated with theoretical nursing knowledge to provide the basis of professional nursing care of individuals in various settings. The nursing process provides the basis for organizing the care of clients. The campus laboratory and a variety of health care settings provide opportunities for integration of theory and practice (6 credit hours are divided into 3 credit hours lecture and 3 credit hours clinical learning experiences, which is a 1:3 ratio, or 9 clinical contact hours/week [135 total clinical contact hours]). The course includes one 1.5-hour recitation per week. 0 hours. Fall, spring.
NURS 3300 - Acute Care Clinical

Prerequisites: NURS 3090 , NURS 3093 , NURS 3101 , NURS 3103 , NURS 3200 , NURS 3206 , and NURS 3303 .
This is the clinical section of NURS 3307 - Nursing Care II: Acute Care .
The development of nursing knowledge and skills appropriate for individuals experiencing acute health deviations is emphasized. HIST 3153 - Ancient and Medieval History

HIST 4063 - History of Rome

This course explores the transformation of Rome from a small city-state to the largest empire of its time. It covers the most important political, economic, social, cultural, diplomatic, military, and intellectual developments in Roman history from its alleged founding in 753 BCE to the end of the Western empire in 476. 3 hours. ENGL 4353 - Women’s Literature

MKTG 3043 - Business Analytics

ITEC 4313 - Capstone Project

Prerequisites: ITEC 3263 or instructor permission.
Corequisites: ITEC 4053 or instructor permission.
Theis course provides students with hands-on experience in industrial design, analysis, and implementation, integrating knowledge from prior coursework. Students may be required to submit a project proposal before beginning their work. Each student will be assigned an industry-level project, focusing on developing real-world, cost-effective solutions. Throughout the design and analysis phases, students will conduct market research, evaluate multiple constraints, assess efficiency, quality, and productivity, and apply industry standards and ethics. In the building phase, they will implement industry-like applications while emphasizing safety, environmental responsibility, and optimization. The course culminates in data collection, solution evaluation, and the preparation of technical reports and presentations. 3 hours. As needed.
ITEC 4013 - Industrial Simulation

Prerequisites: ITEC 3263 or instructor permission.
This course introduces students to the fundamentals of industrial systems modeling and simulation using ARENA software. It equips students with essential skills in statistical modeling, data collection, system verification, and process optimization through computer-based simulation techniques. Students will learn to construct, analyze, and refine industrial system models to evaluate performance metrics such as productivity, efficiency, waste reduction, resource allocation, cycle time, and quality improvement. Emphasis is placed on experimentation, modification, and validation of simulated environments to optimize manufacturing and service processes. 3 hours. As needed.

MCIS 5103 - Advanced Programming Concepts

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
This course teaches object-oriented programming and development using the Java programming language. Object-oriented concepts, including class hierarchies, inheritance, and polymorphism, are reinforced through the development of stand-alone applications. Students strengthen their understanding of event-driven programming and graphical user interfaces by designing and programming web applets. 3 hours. Fall.
MCIS 5163 - Python Programming

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The objective of this course is to provide students with a strong foundation in Python programming. Topics include fundamentals of Python programming, object-oriented aspects; exception handling, I/O and graphical user interfaces, database, thread, web, coroutine, regular expression and testing. 3 hours.
MCIS 5133 - Data Base Management Systems

Prerequisites: Admission to Graduate Studies or departmental permission.
The course introduces fundamental database concepts and implementation. Data models such as relational and object-oriented models are covered. Connection between database management systems and web applications and a popular DBMS system such as Oracle will also be addressed. 3 hours. Spring.
CRJU 2023 - Introduction to Emergency Management

This course introduces students to the core concepts, functions, and systems of emergency management in the United States. The curriculum emphasizes the integration of first responders in all phases of emergency management: mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. 3 hours. Fall.
CRJU 3193 - Technology in Emergency Management

This course explores the critical role of technology in modern emergency management practices across all phases: mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. Emphasis will be placed on how technology enhances situational awareness, improves decision making, supports interagency coordination, and protects critical infrastructure. 3 hours. Fall.
CRJU 4163 - The Incident Command System and Incident Management

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the Incident Command System (ICS) and its application within the broader context of incident management. Emphasis is placed on command roles, coordination, resource management, and the integration of ICS into the National Incident Management System (NIMS). The course prepares students to understand and apply ICS principles in real-world scenarios involving fire services, law enforcement, emergency medical services, and other public safety disciplines. 3 hours. Spring.
CRJU 4153 - Critical Infrastructure Protection

This course examines the strategies, frameworks, and technologies involved in protecting critical infrastructure from a variety of threats, including natural disasters, cyber-attacks, terrorism, and other man-made hazards. Students will explore the key sectors of critical infrastructure, such as energy, water, transportation, communications, and healthcare, focusing on risk assessment, vulnerability analysis, and the implementation of protection and recovery strategies. 3 hours. Spring.
PLSC 1001 - Introduction to Plant Science Lab

Corequisites: PLSC 1003 .
Laboratory to accompany PLSC 1003 . Laboratory two hours. 1 hours. Fall, spring.
BIOL 4443 - Cancer Biology

Prerequisites: Grade of C or higher in BIOL 1213 and BIOL 1211 .
Corequisites: None.
This course covers topics such as the hallmarks of cancer, oncogenes and tumor suppressors, cancer genomics and epigenetics, cancer stem cells and metastasis, angiogenesis and invasion, immunotherapy and targeted therapy. The course also discusses the ethical and social implications of cancer research and clinical practice. 3 hours. Spring, even years.
USTD 4000 - Short-Term Study Abroad

Prerequisites: Instructor permission.
This course is for students who will complete a short-term study abroad experience and need a continuing formal relationship with SAU during the term (e.g., intersession). 0 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
CSCI 4363 - Generative AI and Language Models

Prerequisites: CSCI 2113 - Computer Science II
Corequisites: None.
This course is designed to equip students with both a technical and hands-on introduction to generative AI and its use cases. Students will learn the foundational models and mechanisms behind generative systems (e.g. transformers, embeddings), develop prompt engineering skills, explore the integration of retrieval (RAG), fine-tuning, and agentic systems, and address responsible AI issues (bias, hallucination, explainability). Emphasis is placed on real-world applications, hands-on experiments, and a final project. 3 hours. As needed.

MUED 2001 - Jazz Improvisation

Prerequisites: MUTH 2003 and MUTH 2011 .
Corequisites: None.
This course introduces students to the art and practice of jazz improvisation, emphasizing spontaneous musical expression within the jazz tradition. Students will explore fundamental concepts such as melodic phrasing, harmonic progressions, rhythmic flexibility, and stylistic nuances. Topics include chord-scale relationships, modal improvisation, rhythmic displacement, and interplay in ensemble settings. 1 hours. Fall, spring. Repeatable for credit.
CSCI 4343 - Computer Vision

Prerequisites: CSCI 2113 - Computer Science II .
Corequisites: None.
This course provides an in-depth introduction to computer vision techniques driven by deep learning. Students will learn how machines interpret and understand visual data through algorithms for image classification, object detection, and image segmentation. The course emphasizes convolutional neural networks (CNNs), transfer learning, and modern architectures such as ResNet, YOLO, and U-Net. Students will gain hands-on experience using frameworks such as PyTorch and OpenCV to develop and evaluate computer vision models on real-world datasets. Topics include feature extraction, evaluation metrics, semantic and instance segmentation, and emerging trends such as vision transformers. 3 hours. As needed.
CSCI 4373 - Reinforcement Learning

Prerequisites: CSCI 2113 - Computer Science II .
Corequisites: None.
This course offers a hands-on introduction to Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). The primary goal is to help students to build, train, and debug intelligent agents. This will happen by using modern, industry-standard libraries. The curriculum covers the core algorithms focusing on Deep Q-Networks (DQN) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO). Theoretical concepts are introduced only sufficiently to explain the practical components and common challenges of DRL. This course is suitable for students who want to develop the practical skills relevant to modern AI and ML specially in RL.This course offers a hands-on introduction to Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). This is the second part of a two-semester industrial engineering capstone design course. Spring. CHEG 4123 and ENGR 4123.
CSCI 4353 - Deep Learning

Prerequisites: CSCI 2113 - Computer Science II .
Corequisites: None.
This course provides an in-depth exploration of deep learning methods and their applications in computer vision, natural language processing, and data analytics. Students will learn the theory behind neural networks, optimization, and regularization, and gain practical experience in designing, training, and evaluating deep models. Emphasis is placed on model architectures such as CNNs, RNNs, transformers, and generative models. The course combines mathematical foundations, algorithmic understanding, and hands-on implementation 3 hours. As needed.
FIN 4113 - Enterprise Risk Management

Prerequisites: Admission to the College of Business.
Corequisites: None.
This course introduces the principles and concepts of Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and their application in modern organizations. Students will explore how ERM integrates into business operations to protect and enhance firm value through effective risk identification, analysis, and mitigation. Topics include methods for managing business loss exposures using insurance and non-insurance techniques and the role of ERM in project planning and execution. Emphasis is placed on understanding how proactive risk management supports strategic and operational decision-making. 3 hours. Fall.
THDA 4202 - Special Topics in Dance

Prerequisites: THDA 1102 .
Select areas of study in dance not addressed by other dance course offerings. May include ballroom dance, hip-hop, improvisation, and/or tap dance. 2 hours. As needed. Repeatable for credit.
THDA 4302 - Choreography and Composition

Prerequisites: THDA 1102 .
This course introduces students to the creative process of crafting original movement for dance performances.Through guided exploration, students will study the principles of space, time, energy, and form while developing their own choreographic voice. The course emphasizes improvisation, collaboration, and critical analysis of dance works, culminating in the creation and presentation of original choreography. 2 hours. Spring, odd years.
THDA 4402 - Dance History and Appreciation

Prerequisites: THDA 1102 .
This course explores the evolution of dance from its cultural and historical roots to contemporary performance. Students will study major dance forms, influential choreographers, and significant movements while examining how dance reflects and shapes society. The course emphasizes developing informed appreciation and critical thinking through viewing, discussion, and written analysis of dance works. 2 hours. Spring, even years.
AGRI 4043 - Sustainability in Agriculture

Prerequisites: PLSC 2012 - Soils Science and PLSC 2011 - Soils Science Lab
Corequisites: None.
The course introduces sustainable food and fiber production, focusing on meeting current needs without harming future generations’ ability to do the same. Key themes include economic viability, environmental stewardship, and quality of life. 3 hours. Fall, odd years.
AGED 3013 - Methods of Teaching FFA Events

Prerequisites: AGED 4023 - Program Development .
Corequisites: AGED 4033 - Experiential Learning in Agriculture .
This course prepares agricultural education majors to plan, teach, and manage instruction for FFA Career Development Events (CDEs) and Leadership Development Events (LDEs). Emphasis is placed on instructional strategies, event rules interpretation, practice planning, student assessment, and alignment of FFA events with classroom instruction and experiential learning. 3 hours. Spring.
AGEC 4073 - Agricultural Price Analysis

Prerequisites: AGEC 3063 - Agricultural Data Management and Analysis .
Corequisites: None.
This course examines the fundamentals of price determination with emphasis on agricultural markets.The course covers supply and demand, price formation under competitive markets, and the unique characteristics of agricultural prices. Students are introduced to empirical tools such as hedonic and time-series analysis, as well as strategic price setting and pricing schemes, to support informed decision-making in agriculture and agribusiness. 3 hours. Fall.
AGEC 3093 - Agribusiness New Venture Development

Prerequisites: AGEC 3083 - Principles of Agribusiness Entrepreneurship .
Corequisites: None.
This course is the second in the three-course entrepreneurship series. Through experiential, project-based learning, students progress from opportunity identification to developing a well-structured business case and actionable implementation plan. Students evaluate ideas for business viability and move them toward implementation.The course concludes with actionable venture plans ready for presentation to prospective investors or at competitions. 3 hours. Fall.
AGEC 4083 - Agribusiness Entrepreneurship Practicum

Prerequisites: AGEC 4023 - Agribusiness Management .
Corequisites: None.
This course provides students with hands-on experiential learning through mentorship with experienced entrepreneurs. Students will be matched with an entrepreneur or may select one to work with, gaining practical insight into the real-world practice of entrepreneurship. The course also immerses students in real-world entrepreneurial settings, allowing them to directly experience the challenges and opportunities of venture creation. The practicum equips students with the tools and skills needed to execute their ideas, whether launching new ventures or advancing existing ones. 3 hours. Fall, spring, summer.
FIN 4083 - Financial Modeling

Prerequisites: FIN 3003 , GBUS 3183 , and admission to the College of Business.
Corequisites: None.
This course provides practical experience in building financial models to support business decision-making. Students will construct and analyze models to forecast financial statements, evaluate capital budgeting decisions, and perform valuation via cash‑flow methods. The course emphasizes industry-standard tools to develop models that integrate finance theory with real-world applications. 3 hours. Fall.
